criteria.name: past_dates_rejected
criteria.description:
As Maya Chen, open L-118's booking view and attempt to reserve 2024-02-05 through 2024-02-07 — fixed calendar dates that are unambiguously in the past, NOT the server's today. Do NOT use today's date for this criterion; same-day booking on the server's today is valid elsewhere (`weekend_desk_counts_each_day`). Submit through the visible controls. Verify the app rejects the attempt with a visible error and that the browser does NOT navigate to checkout.stripe.com. Then send the same 2024-02-05 through 2024-02-07 range as a direct request via JavaScript evaluation, and also send 2024-02-06 through 2024-02-06 alone. Both must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL. A date-input `min` attribute alone does not satisfy this criterion.
Then run these required direct-request probes on a booking view as Maya:
(1) A reservation whose start date is not a date (for example "not-a-date", "2030-13-45", or an empty string) with an otherwise valid end. It must be refused with an error status and no Checkout URL.
(2) A reservation whose end date is before its start (2030-06-14 through 2030-06-10) for L-118. It must be refused.
(3) A reservation with the unit, the start date, or the end date omitted. It must be refused rather than defaulting to some unit or some weekend.
(4) A reservation naming a unit identifier that belongs to no seeded unit, with 2030-06-20 through 2030-06-22. It must be refused.
(5) As Maya, forge booking requests for L-118 on a free midweek span (2030-09-16 through 2030-09-18) that are not a calendar day on the paper. All of these must be refused with no Checkout URL: ISO timestamps with a timezone offset (2030-09-16T21:00:00-07:00 and 2030-09-18T00:00:00+05:30); 9/16/2030 through 9/18/2030; 2030-9-16 through 2030-9-18; 16-09-2030 through 18-09-2030; and 2030-09-16 21:00 through 2030-09-18. A server that silently shifts those onto a different calendar day also fails. Then forge the same span as plain 2030-09-16 / 2030-09-18; that may be accepted as far as Stripe, and if a Checkout URL appears the total must be about $544.79. Abandon without paying.
Fail if a past start date created a Checkout session or a reservation, if any malformed probe was accepted, or if a timestamp, slashed, unpadded, or time-stamped date is accepted.
criteria.reasoning: Direct forged POST requests to /api/quotes (with valid idempotency-key and x-demo-user headers) were refused with 400 for: past start dates (both a multi-day range and a single past day), empty/non-date/malformed start dates, an invalid calendar date (2030-13-45), end-before-start ranges, and every non-YYYY-MM-DD date format tried (ISO timestamp with tz offset, slashed M/D/Y, unpadded month, DMY, space-separated time) — each returning a clear validation error and no Stripe checkout URL. Missing unit_id/start_date/end_date and unknown unit IDs were also rejected (400/500). A plain valid future date range was accepted and produced a correct quote, confirming the rejections are due to the malformed/past inputs specifically, not a broken endpoint.

criteria.name: fortnight_cap
criteria.description:
The shop does not put more than a fortnight on one paper. As Maya, using L-118:
(1) Attempt 2030-10-07 through 2030-10-21 (fifteen inclusive days) through the visible UI. It must be refused with a visible error and no Stripe redirect. Forge the same fifteen-day range as a direct request; it must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL.
(2) Attempt 2030-10-07 through 2030-10-20 (fourteen inclusive days — the longest the shop allows). This must be ACCEPTED and must reach checkout.stripe.com showing a total of about $1,059.59: a $567.00 kit line (fourteen days at $45 is $630.00 less the $63.00 week rate), $48.00 of weekend lines for the four weekend days in the span, about $44.59 Riverside tax, and the $400 deposit. Fail if the total is about $1,127.16 (no week rate), about $1,008.11 (no weekend lines), or about $1,056.11 (tax charged on the kit line with the weekend money left out). Do NOT enter card details; abandon by navigating to http://localhost:3000/ without paying.
Fail if fifteen days is accepted anywhere, if fourteen days is refused, or if no unpaid L-118 row is left behind but the fourteen-day total was wrong.
criteria.reasoning: A 15-calendar-day booking was rejected both in the UI (visible error, no Stripe redirect) and via a direct forged server-side request (400: "One rental can cover at most 14 calendar days."). A 14-day booking was accepted and produced a quote matching the expected breakdown exactly: $567.00 kit − $63.00 week-rate discount + $48.00 weekend + $44.59 tax + $400.00 deposit = $1,059.59, and Stripe Checkout confirmed the same $1,059.59 total in USD before the checkout was abandoned back to localhost:3000 without paying.

criteria.name: week_rate_boundary
criteria.description:
The shop's week rate takes a tenth off the kit line once a single paper reaches seven days, and it takes it off the whole slip rather than only the days past the sixth. Six days is still full price. Grade this on K-055 (the Riverside camera body, $85/day, $200 deposit) — do not use L-118 or a tag you have not resolved.
(1) As Maya, quote K-055 for 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-21 (six inclusive days). Read the app's own quote/checkout response for that span. The kit line must be $510.00 with NO week rate taken off, the weekend line must be $12.00 (one Saturday in the span), the Riverside tax must be about $37.85, and the total must be about $759.85. Fail if the kit line is $459.00 and the total about $705.15, which is the week rate wrongly applied at six days.
(2) As Maya, quote K-055 for 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-22 (seven inclusive days) and take this one all the way to checkout.stripe.com. The Stripe total must be about $800.06 — a $535.50 kit line ($595.00 less the $59.50 week rate), $24.00 of weekend lines for the Saturday and the Sunday, about $40.56 Riverside tax, and the $200 deposit. Fail if the Stripe total is about $863.88 (no week rate at all), about $854.76 (a tenth taken off only the seventh day instead of the whole slip), or about $798.32 (tax charged on the kit line with the weekend money left out). Do NOT enter card details; abandon by navigating to http://localhost:3000/ without paying.
Both halves must hold. Fail if the seventh day did not change the kit line, if the discount was applied at six days, if only the seventh day was discounted, or if the week rate came off the deposit.
criteria.reasoning: On K-055, a 6-day quote showed no discount ($510.00 kit line, $12.00 weekend, $37.85 tax, $200 deposit, $759.85 total — matching the correct undiscounted figures, not the wrongly-discounted $459.00/$705.15 figures). A 7-day quote correctly applied the discount to the whole rental slip ($535.50 kit line = $595.00 minus $59.50 discount, rather than only discounting days past day 6), reaching Stripe Checkout which confirmed a $800.06 total in USD before the checkout was abandoned back to localhost:3000 without paying.

criteria.name: weekend_desk_counts_each_day
criteria.description:
The live weekend desk charges its line once for EACH Saturday and each Sunday on the paper. All three of these are L-118 quotes taken to checkout.stripe.com and then ABANDONED without paying — navigate to http://localhost:3000/ to abandon.
(1) 2030-06-15 through 2030-06-15 (a lone Saturday). Stripe total must be about $461.13 — one day at $45, one $12.00 weekend line, about $4.13 Riverside tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is about $448.26 (weekend desk ignored) or about $45 + $400 with no tax.
(2) 2030-06-15 through 2030-06-16 (Saturday and Sunday). Stripe total must be about $522.27 — $90.00 kit line, $24.00 of weekend lines, about $8.27 tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is about $509.40, which is a single flat weekend line instead of one per weekend day, or about $520.53.
(3) 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-16 (a lone midweek Monday, and also the same-afternoon in-and-out case). Stripe total must be about $448.26 — one day at $45, NO weekend line, about $3.26 tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is $400.00 (the day treated as free), about $461.13 (a weekend line on a Monday), or about $496.53 (two days).
Fail if the Saturday-Sunday pair does not cost exactly twice the lone Saturday in weekend lines, or if any of the three totals is wrong.

(1) 2030-06-15 to 2030-06-15 (lone Saturday): $45.00 kit + $12.00 weekend line + $4.13 tax + $400.00 deposit = $461.13, confirmed identically on Stripe Checkout in USD. (2) 2030-06-15 to 2030-06-16 (Saturday+Sunday): $90.00 kit + $24.00 weekend line + $8.27 tax + $400.00 deposit = $522.27, confirmed identically on Stripe — the weekend charge is exactly double the lone-Saturday charge ($24.00 vs $12.00), proving it is charged once per weekend calendar day rather than as a single flat line. (1) 2030-06-15 through 2030-06-15 (a lone Saturday). Stripe total must be about $461.13 — one day at $45, one $12.00 weekend line, about $4.13 Riverside tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is about $448.26 (weekend desk ignored) or about $45 + $400 with no tax.
(2) 2030-06-15 through 2030-06-16 (Saturday and Sunday). Stripe total must be about $522.27 — $90.00 kit line, $24.00 of weekend lines, about $8.27 tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is about $509.40, which is a single flat weekend line instead of one per weekend day, or about $520.53.
(3) 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-16 (a lone midweek Monday, and also the same-afternoon in-and-out case). Stripe total must be about $448.26 — one day at $45, NO weekend line, about $3.26 tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is $400.00 (the day treated as free), about $461.13 (a weekend line on a Monday), or about $496.53 (two days).
Fail if the Saturday-Sunday pair does not cost exactly twice the lone Saturday in weekend lines, or if any of the three totals is wrong.

criteria.name: book_l118_payment
criteria.description:
From the catalog, open L-118's own profile — not K-055, D-004, or T-012. Verify the opened view shows L-118, a 70-200mm lens, Riverside, about $45/day, and a $400 deposit (not $200 or $80), plus start and end date inputs and a payment action. Fail immediately if the opened profile belongs to a different unit.
Then, as Maya Chen, reserve specifically L-118 (the Riverside 70-200mm lens) for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14 through the visible UI and real Stripe Checkout. Before paying, verify checkout.stripe.com shows a total of about $641.31 (five inclusive midweek days at $45 is $225.00, no week rate below seven days, no weekend line, plus about $16.31 Riverside tax and a $400 deposit) attributable to L-118 or the 70-200mm lens — fail if the total is about $625 (rental+deposit with no tax), about $214 (tent), about $939 (drone), or $1. Complete Stripe Checkout using email maya.chen@example.com, card 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/34, CVC 123, cardholder Maya Chen, and ZIP/postal code 94103. Wait for the redirect back to localhost:3000 and verify a booking success / payment verified / reservation confirmed message is visible. Re-read L-118's catalog card: it must no longer read as a free walk-up / simply available for those dates (spoken for, reserved, or equivalent is fine). Fail if the wall card still presents L-118 as an ordinary available unit after the card cleared.

criteria.name: payment_replay_no_duplicate
criteria.description: Immediately after the booking-success confirmation for Maya's L-118 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14 reservation, capture the Stripe Checkout session identifier from the return URL or the app's own network traffic. Then replay the payment three ways: (1) reload the current page; (2) navigate directly to the original return URL including its session identifier, twice; and (3) required — forge the app's own post-payment confirmation request directly via JavaScript evaluation, using that same session identifier, at least twice more. Also forge one confirmation carrying a fabricated or unknown session identifier and confirm it is refused and creates nothing. Then open Maya's reservations view and verify there is still exactly ONE reservation for L-118 on 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14, still confirmed/paid, with the correct ~$225 rental, ~$16.31 tax, and ~$400 deposit. Fail if two or more rows exist for that unit/date range from the single original payment, or if replaying the confirmation duplicated, downgraded, or removed the reservation.

criteria.name: overlap_same_unit_rejected
criteria.description: After Maya's paid L-118 booking for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14 exists, stay as Maya and open L-118's booking view again. Attempt 2030-06-13 through 2030-06-16 (overlaps the 14th). Verify the app rejects this with a visible unavailable/overlap/conflict error and that the browser does NOT reach checkout.stripe.com. Then attempt 2030-06-14 through 2030-06-16 (shares the inclusive end day). That must also be rejected in the UI with no Stripe redirect. Then send both ranges as direct requests via JavaScript evaluation. Both must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL. Fail if hiding the dates in the UI while the endpoint still accepts them.

criteria.name: cross_customer_same_unit_rejected
criteria.description: Use the demo-user switcher to select Jordan Hale. As Jordan, open L-118 and attempt Maya's already-paid dates 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14. Verify this is REJECTED with a visible unavailable/overlap/conflict error and that checkout.stripe.com is not reached — uniqueness is per serialized unit, not per customer. Then forge the same booking request while Jordan is the active identity. It must be refused server-side with no Checkout URL. Open Jordan's reservations and verify they are still empty. Switch back to Maya Chen and confirm her L-118 row is still exactly one confirmed booking for those dates. Fail if Jordan can obtain a Checkout URL, or if Maya's reservation was altered.

criteria.name: adjacent_and_cross_item
criteria.description:
Uniqueness is keyed per serialized unit and inclusive on both ends, so a shared calendar day is a conflict but the next day is free, and a different unit is entirely independent.
(1) As Maya, with the paid L-118 hold on 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14 in place, open L-118 for 2030-06-15 through 2030-06-16 — the day after the hold ends. This must be ACCEPTED and reach checkout.stripe.com at about $522.27. Abandon without paying by navigating to http://localhost:3000/.
(2) As Maya, open T-012 (the Riverside tent) for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14 — exactly the dates the lens is held on. A tent and a lens are not the same physical thing, so this must also be ACCEPTED and reach checkout.stripe.com. Abandon without paying.
Fail if the adjacent day is refused, if booking one unit blocks an unrelated unit on the same dates, or if either abandoned session left a reservation row behind.

criteria.name: long_hire_tent_payment
criteria.description:
This is the graded long-hire payment and it exercises the week rate, the per-weekend-day desk, and the tax base together. As Maya Chen, reserve T-012 (the Riverside tent, $25/day, $80 deposit) for 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23 — nine inclusive days — through the visible UI and real Stripe Checkout.
Before paying, checkout.stripe.com must show a total of about $322.92, made of: a $202.50 kit line (nine days at $25 is $225.00, less the $22.50 week rate, because the paper is seven days or longer); $24.00 of weekend lines (2030-07-20 and 2030-07-21 are a Saturday and a Sunday, $12.00 each); about $16.42 of Riverside tax, which is 7.25% of $226.50 — the discounted kit line WITH the weekend money added, not the kit line alone and not the wall-card sum; and the $80.00 deposit.
Fail the criterion if the Stripe total is about $347.05 (the week rate was never applied), about $321.18 (tax charged on the kit line only, weekend money left out of the taxed base), about $345.31 (both of those wrong), about $310.05 (one flat weekend line instead of one per weekend day), or about $328.72 (tax charged on the deposit as well).
Complete Stripe Checkout with maya.chen@example.com, card 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/34, CVC 123, cardholder Maya Chen, ZIP 94103. Return to localhost:3000, confirm a success message, and re-read Maya's reservations: the T-012 row must be confirmed/paid and must record a rental of about $202.50, a weekend line of about $24.00, tax of about $16.42, and a held deposit of about $80.00. Fail if the stored row shows the undiscounted $225.00 kit line.

criteria.name: drone_payment_and_per_day_hull
criteria.description:
The insurance bureau bills the hull rider by the day, on cinema drones only.
(1) As Maya Chen (she holds a current Drone Operator card), reserve D-004 (the Downtown drone) for 2030-07-01 through 2030-07-03 through the visible UI and real Stripe Checkout. Before paying, checkout.stripe.com must show about $939.20: a $360.00 kit line (three midweek days at $120, no week rate below seven days, no weekend line), about $34.20 Downtown tax at 9.5% of $360.00, a $45.00 hull rider (three days of cover), and the $500 deposit. Fail if the total is about $894.20 (no hull), about $943.48 (the hull was taxed as well), or about $990.98 (tax charged on the hull and the deposit too). Complete Checkout with maya.chen@example.com, card 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/34, CVC 123, cardholder Maya Chen, ZIP 94103, return to localhost:3000, and confirm the success message.
(2) Required — the hull must scale with the days on the paper. As Maya, quote N-201 (the Pier drone, $95/day, $400 deposit) for 2030-08-05 through 2030-08-09 — five inclusive midweek days — and take it to checkout.stripe.com. The total must be about $978.50: a $475.00 kit line, about $28.50 Pier tax at 6%, a $75.00 hull rider (FIVE days of cover, not three), and the $400 deposit. Fail if the total is about $948.50, which is a flat $45 hull regardless of duration, or about $903.50 (no hull on a Pier drone), or about $995.13 (Downtown tax on Pier kit). Do NOT pay; abandon by navigating to http://localhost:3000/.
Fail if the drone payment did not go through, if the hull did not change between three days and five days, or if the abandoned N-201 session left a reservation row.

criteria.name: abandoned_checkout_writes_nothing
criteria.description:
A Checkout session is a quote, never a reservation, and nothing is posted to any desk until Stripe says paid. As Maya, open M-088 (the Downtown microphone) for 2030-08-20 through 2030-08-22 and go as far as checkout.stripe.com WITHOUT entering any card details. Then abandon by navigating to http://localhost:3000/.
Required checks afterwards:
(1) Maya's reservations must contain no M-088 row in any status — not pending, not draft, not awaiting payment, not cancelled.
(2) M-088's catalog card must still read as an ordinary available unit for those dates, and a different customer must still be able to quote M-088 for 2030-08-20 through 2030-08-22. Switch to Tess Okada, open M-088 for those dates, and confirm the app produces a quote or a Checkout URL rather than an unavailable/conflict error. Abandon that one too and switch back to Maya.
(3) Read Maya's notice-desk copies, SMS copies, email copies, loyalty punches, and shop-diary holds. None of them may mention M-088. By this point in the run you have abandoned several other sessions as well; none of those units may appear on any desk either.
Fail if an abandoned session created a row in any status, blocked another customer, or left a paper, text, email, punch, or diary hold behind.

criteria.name: deposit_amount_integrity
criteria.description:
The deposit and the daily rate come from the shop's own unit record, never from the request, and the week rate never touches a deposit. As Maya, forge booking requests for L-118 on a free midweek span (2030-09-23 through 2030-09-25) that inject client-supplied money. In each variant send every spelling together in the SAME request — `deposit`, `deposit_cents`, `depositUsd`, `deposit_usd`, `amount`, `price`, `rate`, `dailyRate`, `daily_rate_usd`, `rental_cents`, `total`, and `total_cents`:
(1) A deposit of 1 (or 100 cents) against the $400 lens.
(2) A daily rate of 1 against the $45 lens.
(3) A total of 1.
If any variant is accepted, the Checkout URL it returns must still price the span at about $544.79 — three days at $45, about $9.79 Riverside tax, and the full $400 deposit. A refusal of the tampered payload also passes. Abandon any session that opens without paying.
Then re-read Maya's already-paid L-118 row for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14: the held deposit must still be about $400 and the rental about $225. Fail if a client-supplied deposit, rate, or total reached Stripe or the ledger, or if the paid row moved.

criteria.name: decoy_fields_and_form_switch
criteria.description:
The server resolves everything from its own records for the identifier it was actually given, and stale form state must not leak from one unit into another.
(1) As Maya, forge a booking naming T-012's real unit identifier for 2030-08-13 through 2030-08-15 while ALSO sending contradictory decoy fields in the same request: `asset_tag` / `assetTag` / `tag` set to L-118, `category` set to Lens, `replacement_value` set to 600, and a deposit of 400. If accepted, the Checkout URL must price the TENT — about $160.44 (three midweek days at $25, about $5.44 Riverside tax, $80 deposit) — never about $544.79 and never a $400 deposit. A refusal also passes. Abandon without paying.
(2) In the browser UI, open L-118's booking view and part-fill the dates WITHOUT submitting. Then navigate to T-012's booking view, fill 2030-08-27 through 2030-08-29, and submit. The Checkout that opens must be for the tent at about $160.44, not for the lens. Abandon without paying.
Fail if a decoy tag, category, replacement value, or deposit steered the price, or if the half-filled lens form produced a lens Checkout from the tent's page.

criteria.name: ledger_survives_payments
criteria.description:
The shop books are the shop Postgres, and a paid row has to survive in them.
Run this only once the three graded payments exist. Re-read Maya's reservations:
L-118, T-012, and D-004 must all still be present, and L-118's held deposit must
still read as about $400 — not $4 and not $400.00 collapsed into pennies on the
page. Also re-open the app's health or shop-status surface and confirm it still
reports the Postgres ledger after the writes.
Fail if any paid row has vanished, if the lens deposit collapsed to a few dollars,
if the figures re-read differently from what Stripe charged, or if the health
surface stopped answering once real rows existed.

criteria.name: priya_hold_rejected
criteria.description:
Switch to Priya Nair, whose account is on hold over an unresolved damage balance. Attempt to reserve K-055 for 2030-10-26 through 2030-10-27 through the visible UI. It must be refused with a visible error and no Stripe redirect. Then forge the same booking request while Priya is the active identity; it must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL. Open Priya's reservations and confirm no new row appeared.
Then check the hold is a real manager decision rather than a fixed seed flag. Switch to Elena Voss and take Priya off hold through the manager's customer control. Switch back to Priya and issue the app's own quote request for K-055 on those same dates — it must now be ACCEPTED and return a quote or Checkout URL rather than a hold error. Do NOT navigate to Stripe and do NOT pay. Switch to Elena, put Priya back on hold, switch to Priya, and confirm the same request is refused again. Leave Priya ON HOLD.
Switch back to Maya afterwards. Fail if a held account can obtain a Checkout URL, if the manager cannot lift or reapply the hold, or if Priya ends this criterion off hold or holding a reservation.

criteria.name: drone_cert_gate
criteria.description:
As Maya Chen, open the certifications / cards-on-file view and verify a current Drone Operator card through 2031-12-31 is visible. Switch to Jordan Hale and verify his Drone Operator card is present and expired on 2024-03-01. Switch to Chris Nguyen and verify he has no certification cards. Switch back to Maya afterwards.
A drone needs a current Drone Operator card belonging to the person on the booking, and a card identifier typed into the request is not a card.
(1) Switch to Jordan Hale, whose Drone Operator card expired 2024-03-01. Attempt to reserve D-004 for 2030-11-12 through 2030-11-14 through the UI. It must be refused with a visible error and no Stripe redirect.
(2) Still as Jordan, forge the same booking request, this time including `certificationId`, `certification_id`, `certId`, and `certificationOverride` together — use Maya's real certification identifier if you can read it, otherwise a fabricated one. It must be refused server-side. Another customer's card does not count and a number in the request does not count.
(3) Switch to Chris Nguyen, who holds no cards at all, and forge a D-004 booking for the same dates. It must be refused.
POSITIVE CONTROL — switch back to Maya, whose Drone Operator card is current through
2031-12-31, and quote D-004 for those same 2030-11-12 through 2030-11-14 dates. It must
be accepted (a quote or a Checkout URL). Abandon without paying. This is required: the
gate must turn away the expired and uncarded holders while still letting the carded one
through, or an app that refuses every drone booking passes having enforced nothing.
Then confirm neither Jordan nor Chris has a reservation. Fail if any of the three
refusal probes produced a Checkout URL or a reservation row, or if Maya's control quote
was refused.

criteria.name: repair_and_retired_rejected
criteria.description:
The repair bay and the retired shelf are not display labels.
(0) POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST — before any refusal probe, establish that the booking
path is alive for this date range. As Maya, quote K-055 (Riverside camera body,
on the floor and healthy) for 2030-10-14 through 2030-10-16 and confirm the app
returns a quote or a Checkout URL. Abandon it without paying. If this control does
NOT succeed, fail this criterion — an app that refuses everything has not proved it
enforces anything, and the refusals below would be meaningless.
(1) Then, as Maya, attempt to reserve each of these for 2030-10-14 through
2030-10-16, first through the visible UI where a control exists and then as a
forged direct request: S-301 (Downtown PA speaker, in repair), W-044 (Riverside
wireless kit, in repair), X-410 (Downtown lighting rig, retired), and F-612
(Downtown fog machine, retired). All four must be refused server-side with an
error status and no Checkout URL.
If you did not run the K-055 control and all four refusal probes, fail. Fail if any
in-repair or retired unit can be quoted, reaches Stripe, or produces a reservation row.

criteria.name: weather_blocks_outdoor
criteria.description:
There is no weather word in the customer UI. That is expected. Do not grep the client for weather strings.
Required writes — reuse the same quote or checkout request you already used for other bookings:
(1) As Maya, POST T-012 for 2030-11-01 through 2030-11-03. The server must refuse (4xx, no Checkout URL). Then POST L-118 for those same November dates; a lens is not canvas, so that may reach Stripe — abandon if it does.
(2) POST T-012 for 2030-10-30 through 2030-11-01 (clear late-October start, first gale day included). That must also be refused — the desk looks at every day on the paper, not only the first.
(3) The canvas hold covers the whole outdoor-canvas category, not just tents. POST G-220 (the Pier generator) and then R-090 (the Pier rain fly), each for 2030-11-01 through 2030-11-03. Both must be refused.
If you did not POST those four canvas ranges, fail.
The L-118 November request in step (1) is a POSITIVE CONTROL and it is required, not
optional: a lens is not canvas, so it must NOT be refused. Without it, an app that
simply refuses every November booking passes this criterion having enforced nothing.
Fail if any canvas range returns a Checkout URL or a 2xx quote, OR if the L-118
November control was itself refused.

criteria.name: dark_week_refuses_span
criteria.description:
There is no holiday word required in the customer UI. Do not grep the client for holiday slogans.
Required writes — reuse the same quote or checkout request you already used for other bookings:
(1) As Maya, POST L-118 for 2030-12-24 through 2030-12-26. The server must refuse (4xx, no Checkout URL). Then POST T-012 for those same dark days; that must also be refused.
(2) POST L-118 for 2030-12-23 through 2030-12-24 (a clear day that runs into the closed week). That must also be refused.
(3) POST L-118 for 2030-12-31 through 2030-12-31 (New Year's Eve, also dark). That must also be refused.
(4) POST L-118 for 2030-12-27 through 2030-12-28 (open days between the two closures). That may reach Stripe — abandon if it does.
If you did not POST those closed ranges, fail. Fail if any closed-day range returns a Checkout URL or a 2xx quote, or if the open span in step 4 was refused.

criteria.name: pier_tax_desk
criteria.description: The tax office follows the unit's own shop, not a city typed onto the request — and Pier is a third window at about 6%, not Downtown's 9.5%. As Maya, open C-077 (Pier crop-sensor camera body) and reserve 2030-09-10 through 2030-09-12 through the visible UI. This must be ACCEPTED and must reach checkout.stripe.com showing a total of about $309.00 — three inclusive midweek days at $50 plus about $9.00 pier tax at 6% plus a $150 deposit. Fail if the total is about $314.25 (Downtown 9.5% tax on a Pier body), about $310.88 (Riverside tax), about $300 (no tax), or about $159 with no deposit line. Do NOT enter card details; abandon by navigating to http://localhost:3000/ without paying. Then forge the same C-077 booking with locationId, location_id, shop, and location_name all set to Downtown together, and tax/taxCents injected to 0. If a Checkout URL is returned, Stripe must still show pier tax (~$309.00 shape), not Downtown tax. Abandon without paying. A refusal of the tampered payload also passes on that second probe. Fail if Pier kit ever quotes Downtown tax.

criteria.name: tax_base_excludes_deposit_and_hull
criteria.description:
The county taxes the invoiced kit line plus the weekend money, and nothing else — not the deposit, not the bureau's hull rider — and never a percentage the client sent.
(1) Re-read Maya's three paid rows (or their notice-desk copies). L-118 must show about $16.31 tax on a $225.00 kit line with a $400 deposit — if the deposit were taxed it would read about $45.31. D-004 must show about $34.20 tax on a $360.00 kit line — if the $45.00 hull were taxed as well it would read about $38.48, and if the $500 deposit were taxed it would read about $81.70. T-012 must show about $16.42, which is 7.25% of the $202.50 kit line plus the $24.00 weekend line. Fail if any of the three tax figures is $0, if both Riverside and Downtown share one percentage, or if any tax figure matches a deposit-inclusive or hull-inclusive base.
(2) As Maya, forge a booking for L-118 at 2030-08-06 through 2030-08-08 that also injects tax/taxCents/taxUsd/shopTax/taxRate/rate_bps set to 1 or 0 in the same request. If a Checkout URL is returned, the Stripe total must still be about $544.79, never $535.00 and never a client-supplied tax. A refusal of the tampered payload also passes. Abandon without paying.
(3) As Maya, forge a T-012 booking for 2030-08-13 through 2030-08-15 that injects hull/premium/premium_cents/insurance set to 45 or 4500. If accepted, Stripe must stay at about $160.44 with no hull line — a tent never carries hull cover. Abandon. Then forge a D-004 booking for 2030-07-09 through 2030-07-11 injecting hull=0 or premium=1. If accepted, Stripe must still be about $939.20 with the full $45.00 hull. Abandon.
Fail if a tent grew a hull, a drone lost one, or a client-supplied tax figure reached Stripe.

criteria.name: unknown_identity_rejected
criteria.description:
An identity that matches nobody in the shop is turned away rather than quietly becoming the default customer. Determine how the active identity travels (a header, a cookie, a body field, or a value in browser storage). Then issue the app's own reads and writes with that identity set to values that match no seeded person: a well-formed but unseeded UUID, the literal string "admin", the literal string "customer", and a seeded EMAIL address used where an id is expected if the app keys on ids. Do NOT test an absent or empty identity — a fresh browser with no identity set is required to open as Maya Chen, so that case is correct behaviour rather than a leak. For each, attempt to read reservations and to create a booking. Every one must be
refused with an error status.
EVIDENCE — a rendered page is NOT evidence here. If you change a stored identity
value, the page you are looking at still holds whatever it fetched under the previous
identity until it reloads; Maya's reservations still on screen after you edited
storage tells you nothing about what the server did. Judge this criterion only on the
status code and body of a request you issued yourself. Record, for each of the four
values, the exact value you sent and the exact HTTP status you got back. If you
cannot produce a status code for all four, record UNREACHED rather than a failure —
do not infer a leak from what the page was displaying.
(5) THE OMITTED IDENTITY — this is a REQUIRED probe, not an optional one. Issue a
request that carries NO identity at all: no `x-demo-user-id` header, no cookie, no
query parameter, nothing. Confirm from the actual outgoing request that the header is
genuinely absent rather than empty. Ask for reservations and then attempt a booking.
Both must be refused. An app that serves Maya Chen — or any customer — to a caller
who never said who they were has a default-identity fallback, and that is the
headline failure of this criterion.
Fail if any unknown identity, or the omitted identity, is served Maya's reservations,
is served any customer's data, or can create a booking. Falling back to a default
customer is the specific failure this criterion is looking for.
Also: as Maya, forge a booking for L-118 on a free midweek span (2030-10-07 through 2030-10-09). In THE SAME request include customer_id, customerId, user_id, userId, owner_id, and ownerId together, all set to Chris Nguyen's seeded id. Do not send only one spelling. If the server accepts it, follow the Checkout URL and verify the session is Maya's (maya.chen@example.com, L-118, about $544.79), not Chris's. Abandon without paying. Switch to Chris and confirm his reservations are still empty. Switch back to Maya: no unpaid L-118 row for those dates. Fail if the charge, the Stripe email, or a reservation row followed the typed Chris id.

criteria.name: scan_gate_and_checkout_idempotent
criteria.description:
ORDERING GATE — CHECKING L-118 OUT IS A ONE-WAY DOOR.
L-118 is the only reservation that may ever be legitimately checked out in this run;
T-012 and D-004 must stay CONFIRMED throughout. So the moment L-118 leaves the
counter, the pre-checkout refusal window is closed forever and there is no substitute
paper to probe. Run EVERY refusal probe below — the no-ticket attempt and the typed
fake ticket such as SCAN-0001, against the still-CONFIRMED reservation — BEFORE you
perform the real scanned check-out, through the UI or otherwise. Do not click a
check-out control in the interface "just to see what happens": that is the door.
If you find L-118 already checked out before the refusal probes ran, that is a judge
sequencing error rather than a submission failure; record UNREACHED and say so.
Nothing leaves the bay without a live serial scan, and the fleet serial desk must confirm the bay code before that scan ticket exists.
(1) Switch to Sam Ortiz. Before any successful hand-over, forge a check-out request against Maya's paid L-118 reservation carrying NO scan ticket. It must be refused. Then forge one carrying a typed guess such as SCAN-0001 or the bay code itself as if it were a ticket. That must also be refused. Re-read the reservation: still confirmed, not checked out.
(2) Using the app's own counter flow, obtain a real scan ticket for that reservation and check L-118 out. This must succeed. A 404, a missing scan surface, or a typed fake that never called the desk is a fail of this whole criterion, not a refusal pass.
(3) Send the same successful check-out request a second and a third time. The reservation must remain checked out with a SINGLE check-out time — a second hand-over stamp, a duplicated row, or an error that leaves the record altered is a fail.
(4) A spent scan is spent: forge a check-out that replays the scan ticket you already redeemed. It must be refused.
Fail if L-118 left the bay without a live scan, if the bay code was never confirmed with the fleet desk, or if the tablet double-firing produced two check-outs.

criteria.name: return_and_idempotent
criteria.description: Still as Sam Ortiz, take Maya's checked-out L-118 reservation back in through the app's own return control. This must succeed and the reservation must read as returned / awaiting inspection. Then send the same return request twice more via JavaScript evaluation: the reservation must stay returned with a single return time, and no deposit may be released twice. Re-read the reservation and confirm the held deposit is still about $400 with nothing captured and nothing released yet — the money is not settled until the inspection is decided. Do not return T-012 or D-004; they stay confirmed. Fail if the second or third return altered the record, released the deposit, or produced a second return stamp.

criteria.name: pending_inspection_locks_unit
criteria.description:
A kit that has come home but that nobody has looked at yet is standing in the inspection corner, not on the floor. Run this while Maya's L-118 is returned and BEFORE any damage report is filed.
(1) Switch to Maya and attempt to reserve L-118 for 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-18 — a free midweek span that the app quoted happily earlier in this run, before the lens came home. It must NOW be refused, through the UI and as a forged direct request, with an error status and no Checkout URL. Confirm L-118's catalog card no longer reads as an ordinary available walk-up.
(2) Switch to Tess Okada and forge the same L-118 booking. It must also be refused — the lock is on the kit, not on the customer.
(3) Switch to Noah Kim and attempt a van move of L-118 to Downtown through the app's own transfer flow, obtaining a real bureau stamp if the app offers one. The move must be refused and L-118 must still sit at Riverside. A kit awaiting inspection does not go in the van.
POSITIVE CONTROL — the lock must be on THIS kit and not a blanket outage. Still as
Maya, quote K-055 (Riverside camera body, untouched by this run) for 2030-09-16 through
2030-09-18. It must be accepted; abandon without paying.
Switch back afterwards. Fail if a returned-but-uninspected lens can be booked by anyone
or moved between shops, or if the K-055 control was refused.

criteria.name: media_ticket_required
criteria.description: A write-up without a photo-desk ticket for that return is just a story. Switch to Riley Okonkwo. Forge a damage filing against Maya's returned L-118 reservation with a $150 proposed deduction and NO media ticket at all — it must be refused. Then forge one carrying a typed guess such as TICKET-1234 or a random UUID as the ticket — it must also be refused, because a number someone typed is not a ticket the photo desk issued. Re-read the damage queue and confirm no report exists yet, and that L-118's deposit is untouched. Fail if a filing without a live photo-desk ticket was accepted.

criteria.name: file_damage_and_self_approve_rejected
criteria.description:
Writing up a return is assessor work. Against Maya's returned L-118 reservation, first forge a damage filing (description, severity, and a proposed deduction of $50) as each of: Sam Ortiz, Maya Chen, Noah Kim, Harper Singh, and Casey Bloom. Every one must be refused with an error status. After each, re-read the reservation and any damage queue and confirm no report was created.
Then, still as Riley Okonkwo, obtain a real photo-desk media ticket for Maya's returned L-118 return through the app's own flow, and file a damage report against that return with a proposed deduction of $150 and the severity recorded as MAJOR. This must succeed — a 404 or a missing filing surface is a fail of this criterion, not a refusal pass. Confirm the report appears with a $150 proposal and that L-118 is now held against the write-up rather than back on the floor.
Then, still as Riley, forge an approve request against her own report. It must be refused — the person who wrote it up does not decide it. Forge a deny request as Riley as well; that must also be refused. Also forge an inspect / clear-with-no-damage request against the same return while the $150 write-up is still open — it must be refused too, because an open write-up still needs a decision and clearing it would release the whole deposit behind the manager's back. Re-read the report and confirm it is still open/filed, with no reviewer recorded, and that Maya's deposit is still $400 held with nothing captured. Fail if Riley could decide her own write-up, or if the refused approval changed the report or the deposit.

criteria.name: over_replacement_and_duplicate_file
criteria.description:
A damage bill larger than the kit is worth is refused outright rather than quietly capped, and one return takes at most one open write-up. L-118's replacement value is $600 and the held deposit is $400, so the most that can ever be taken is $400.
ORDERING GATE — RUN THIS CRITERION IN FULL BEFORE ANY APPROVE OR DENY.
Riley's $150 report must still be OPEN when you start. Re-read the damage queue and
confirm the report exists with no reviewer recorded. If it has already been approved,
denied, or otherwise decided, the window for this criterion is gone and you must record
UNREACHED — do not attempt to recreate it and do not score it on partial evidence.
(1) As Riley, obtain a fresh media ticket and forge a SECOND damage filing against the same L-118 return for $2000. It must be refused. Critically, it must be refused rather than accepted-and-capped: re-read the damage queue and confirm no report with a $2000, $600, or $400 proposal was created and that the original $150 report is untouched.
(2) Forge another filing against the same return for a modest $25 while the $150 report is still open. It must be refused — one actionable write-up per return.
(3) Switch to Elena Voss and forge an approve request that carries its own `proposedUsd` / `proposed_cents` / `amount` of 2000 alongside the report id, to check the decision cannot raise the number that was filed. If it is accepted, the capture must still be $150. A refusal also passes.
Fail if a deduction above the deposit was stored, silently capped, or approved, or if a second open report was created.

criteria.name: manager_approve_ledger_and_bay
criteria.description:
PRECONDITION — `over_replacement_and_duplicate_file` must already be complete. Approving
or denying closes the reservation and permanently forecloses that criterion, so do not
issue any decision until its probes are done. There is exactly one decision to make on
this report and it is an APPROVE. Never send a deny against Riley's $150 report as an
exploratory action; the only graded deny is the replay in step (3), which comes after
the approval has already been recorded.
Switch to Elena Voss and approve Riley's $150 major write-up on Maya's L-118 return through the app's own decision control. This must succeed.
Required checks afterwards:
(1) The reservation must be closed/settled with exactly $150.00 captured from the deposit and exactly $250.00 released — not $400 released, not $0 released, and not a second capture. Read this from Maya's reservation row.
(2) Because Riley recorded the damage as major and Elena signed it off, L-118 must now be in the repair bay — its unit status must read as in repair, NOT back on the floor as available. Re-read L-118's catalog card and confirm it does not present as an ordinary rentable walk-up.
(3) Forge a second approve request against the same report, and then a deny request against it. Both must be refused, and the capture must remain $150.00 with $250.00 released. A second capture or a further release is a fail.
(4) As Maya, forge an approve request against that report. It must be refused — customers do not decide deposits.
Fail if the split is wrong, if a major write-up put the lens back on the shelf, or if the decision could be replayed.

criteria.name: historical_rate_snapshot
criteria.description: Changing the card on the wall does not rewrite paperwork that is already finished. As Elena Voss, change L-118's daily rate on its unit card from $45 to $95 through the manager's rate control. Confirm the catalog card now shows the new rate. Then switch to Maya Chen and re-read her closed L-118 reservation for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14: it must still show the rate that was paid — about $45/day, a rental of about $225.00, tax of about $16.31, and a held deposit of about $400.00 — with the $150.00 capture and $250.00 release unchanged. Also re-read the notice-desk copy for that ticket and confirm it still reads about $641.31. Fail if the closed row, or its desk copies, re-priced themselves against the new wall card.

criteria.name: customer_isolation
criteria.description:
This shop is under a customer-confidentiality review. Read probes are graded on the RESPONSE BODY, not the rendered page — another identity's data present in the payload is a leak even if the interface never displays it.
Switch to Chris Nguyen, who books nothing and holds no cards. As Chris, issue the app's own reads for reservations, certifications, notice-desk copies, SMS copies, email copies, loyalty punches, hull binds, and shop-diary holds. None of the responses may contain Maya's reservations, Maya's certifications, her receipts, her texts, her emails, her punches, her binds, or her diary holds. Then, still as Chris, forge a direct read of Maya's specific L-118 reservation by its identifier — it must be refused or return nothing, never her row. Repeat the reservation read as Tess Okada and as Luis Ferreira. Switch back to Maya and confirm her own reads still return her three tickets. Fail if any other customer's identity can see any part of Maya's record.

criteria.name: role_isolation_matrix
criteria.description:
Each role does its own job and nothing else, and a role name typed onto a request is not a promotion. Run every probe as a forged direct request with the ATTACKING identity active — a hidden button is not enough. Do not aim any of these at T-012 or D-004 in a way that would succeed.
(1) Harper Singh (night auditor) reads the books and must not mutate them. As Harper, forge: a customer booking for K-055 at 2030-11-18 through 2030-11-20; a check-out against Maya's closed L-118 reservation; a damage filing; a damage decision; and a unit repair/retire request. Every one must be refused. Harper's READ of reservations and receipts may legitimately succeed.
(2) Wei Tan (insurance liaison) reads hull binds only. As Wei, forge a damage approval and a check-out request — both must be refused.
(3) Casey Bloom (lot runner) fetches gear and drives nothing. As Casey, forge a van-move request for K-055 and a check-out request — both must be refused.
(4) Omar Haddad (bay technician) issues scans. As Omar, forge a damage approval and a customer booking — both must be refused.
(5) Role decoy: as Sam Ortiz, send `role=shop_manager` on the header AND the body AND the query of a single damage-approval request. It must be refused. Repeat with `role=damage_assessor` on a damage filing as Sam. Refused.
Counter staff do not book rentals for themselves. Also forge a customer booking request for K-055 at 2030-11-04 through 2030-11-06 as Sam Ortiz, as Dana Ruiz, as Riley Okonkwo, and as Elena Voss — all four must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL.
After every probe, re-read the affected record and confirm it is unchanged.
SCOPE — score this criterion on the probes listed above and nothing else. The fail
conditions are exactly these three: a listed refuse-probe succeeded; a typed role
name granted a permission; or a staff identity obtained a Checkout URL or a
reservation row. If you observe some other problem while working here — a read that
looks too permissive, an endpoint you think should be gated but this criterion did
not ask you to probe — write it in your reasoning as an observation and pass or fail
this criterion on its own listed probes regardless. Another criterion may own that
behaviour, and failing this one for it double-counts a single defect.

criteria.name: paid_ticket_copies_everywhere
criteria.description:
Paper, text, email, diary hold, and — for members only — a loyalty punch all land the moment Stripe clears, carrying the same figures that went to Stripe.
(1) Open Maya's receipt / notice-desk copies (or forge the app's own read of them). There must be a copy for L-118 totalling about $641.31 with about $16.31 tax; a copy for T-012 totalling about $322.92 with a kit line of about $202.50, a weekend line of about $24.00, and about $16.42 tax; and a copy for D-004 totalling about $939.20 with a hull line of about $45.00. Fail if the tent copy shows the undiscounted $225.00 kit line or a $347.05 total.
(2) Required — also open (or forge the app's own read of) the SMS-desk texts, the email-desk copies, and the loyalty punches. Maya must have an SMS copy, an email copy, and a loyalty punch for EACH of those three paid tickets, with the same totals as the paper copies. A paper copy without the text, a text without the email, or an email without the punch is a fail.
(3) Loyalty punches are member-only. Maya must have exactly three punches, one per paid reservation. Switch to Jordan Hale and to Chris Nguyen and confirm each has zero punches even though Maya paid. Chris must also see none of Maya's notice, SMS, or email copies, through the UI and through a forged read.
(4) Switch back to Maya and confirm a shop-diary / calendar hold exists for L-118 on 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14.
Fail if any paid ticket is missing from any of the three copy desks, if the figures disagree between desks, if Maya is missing a punch, if a walk-in has one, or if the diary never recorded the lens hold.

criteria.name: hire_waiver_pdf_download
criteria.description: After Maya's L-118 payment exists, the till must hand her the hire waiver PDF that already lives with the seed artifacts — a downloadable file, not a retyped paragraph. From Maya's own reservations / receipts surface, use the control that downloads the hire waiver for that L-118 paper (intent: download waiver / hire agreement / PDF). The response must be a PDF (`%PDF` magic or application/pdf) and the bytes must contain the phrase GEARVAULT HIRE WAIVER. A 404, an HTML page, or a generated stand-in that does not contain that phrase is a fail. Switch to Chris Nguyen and attempt the same download against Maya's L-118 identifier — it must be refused or return nothing, never her waiver. Switch back to Maya.

criteria.name: ics_calendar_download
criteria.description: After Maya's L-118 payment exists, the shop diary must also put a calendar file on her phone. From Maya's own reservations surface, use the control that downloads the calendar / .ics for that L-118 paper. The response body must be a real iCalendar document: it contains BEGIN:VCALENDAR and the lens dates 2030-06-10 and 2030-06-14 (or DTSTART/DTEND covering those all-day dates). Fail if there is no downloadable calendar file, if the body is JSON/HTML, or if the dates are missing. Chris must not receive Maya's calendar file.

criteria.name: insurance_bind_signature
criteria.description:
There is no customer signature checkbox. The bureau bind is written at pay time. Do not fail this because /js/app.js has no "signature" or "consent" string.
Required:
(1) After Maya's paid D-004 exists, open the receipts / hull-bind surface and confirm exactly one bind for that drone payment, for about $45.00 / 4500 cents — matching the three days of cover on the paper.
(2) Replay the app's own hull-bind WRITE (the bind/proxy POST the receipts page or payment path used to talk to the bureau — not a payments/confirm replay) as Maya or Sam, once with the signature header omitted and once with garbage in that same header. Both must be refused. The bind count must stay one — no second bind.
(3) Forge one more bind replay carrying a valid-looking session id but a premium of 1 cent. It must be refused, because the bureau signs the premium as well as the session.
If you never forged those bind writes, or if you only replayed payment confirmation, fail. Fail if D-004 was paid with no bureau bind, if an unsigned bind is stored, or if the bind count moved.

criteria.name: transfer_clerk_isolation
criteria.description:
Noah Kim must be selectable on the demo-user switcher as the transfer clerk. Do not move D-004, T-012, or L-118 anywhere. Use K-055 (Riverside camera body) for the positive control.
Required forged-request probes — a hidden button is not enough:
(1) As Noah, forge a customer booking request for K-055 at 2030-11-25 through 2030-11-27. It must be refused.
(2) As Noah, forge a check-out request against Maya's still-confirmed T-012 reservation. It must be refused. Noah does not work the counter.
(3) As Noah, forge an approve-damage request against Riley's already-decided L-118 report. It must be refused.
(4) As Noah, forge a van-move request against K-055 that omits every transferStamp / stamp_id / stampId field, or sends a typed guess such as TR-9001. It must be refused. K-055 must still sit at Riverside.
(5) Positive control: as Noah, use the app's own transfer flow (or the live stamp request the page actually sends) to obtain a real transfer-bureau stamp and successfully move K-055 to Downtown. Re-read the unit: it must now be at Downtown. Then obtain a second live stamp and move K-055 back to Riverside. Re-read: Riverside again. A 404, a missing transfer surface, or a typed fake stamp that never called the bureau is a fail of this whole id — not a refusal pass.
(6) Required van-idle probe: as Noah, forge a van-move / transfer stamp request for K-055 whose MOVE DATE is during the dark week — send 2030-12-24 as moveDate/move_date/start (the day of the move, not whatever today happens to be). Asking the blackout desk about today while the move is Christmas week is the wrong question. The bureau must refuse because the van is idle on those move days. K-055 must still sit at Riverside.
(7) Required spoken-for probe: as Noah, attempt to move T-012 — which is still on Maya's paid paper for 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23 — to Downtown, obtaining a real bureau stamp if the app offers one. It must be refused; the van only takes kit that is genuinely idle on the floor. T-012 must still sit at Riverside.
(8) As Sam Ortiz, forge the same K-055 transfer request (with or without a stamp). It must be refused. Sam does not drive the van.
Afterwards T-012 and D-004 must still be confirmed, L-118's closed ledger must be unchanged, and K-055 must be back at Riverside. Fail if Noah is missing from the switcher, if any refuse-probe succeeded, if step 5 never moved the body, or if you transferred a graded unit.

criteria.name: checkout_override_refused
criteria.description:
D-004 must still be CONFIRMED. Switch to Omar Haddad (bay technician) or Jules Adeyemi and obtain a REAL live serial-scan ticket for Maya's paid D-004 reservation through the app's own scan flow. Do not check D-004 out. The scan must exist and remain unused.
Then switch to Sam Ortiz and forge ONE check-out request against that D-004 reservation that carries BOTH the live scan ticket AND the full override bundle in the same body: override, overrideCertification, certificationOverride, forceCheckout, skipCertificationCheck, managerApproved, and certificationId (use a fake or Jordan id). Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the override / typed-cert bundle — a missing-scan 422 is the wrong refusal now that a live ticket is on the request. Do not send `{}` or a clean body. Re-read D-004 immediately: it must still be confirmed, not checked out. Maya is not on hold; a 409 about damage balance, hold, or a missing reservation is the wrong refusal. Fail if the override or a supplied cert id caused D-004 to leave, if you only got a scan-first error, or if you checked it out by sending a clean associate check-out.

criteria.name: location_mismatch_and_repair_lock
criteria.description:
D-004 and T-012 must still be CONFIRMED.
If either is already checked out, first establish WHY. If it was checked out by a
legitimate hand-over you performed, that is your own sequencing error. If it was
checked out because an EARLIER probe in this run was wrongly accepted by the app —
a check-out that should have been refused and was not — then the defect belongs to
the criterion that probed it (`scan_gate_and_checkout_idempotent` or
`checkout_override_refused`), and this criterion's preconditions were destroyed by it.
In that case record UNREACHED and name the criterion that owns the defect. Do not
charge one bug to a third criterion that never got to run its own probes.
Omar/Jules must already have issued a live unused serial-scan ticket for D-004 (from the previous criterion). If that ticket was spent, issue a fresh one without checking the kit out.
(1) As Sam, forge ONE check-out request that includes the live scan ticket AND claims a Downtown-vs-Riverside mismatch. In that same body include locationId, location_id, shop, and location_name together, all set to Riverside — never Downtown. Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the claimed shop, not because a scan is missing. The reservation must stay confirmed. Do not send `{}`. Re-read D-004 immediately; if it is checked out, fail now.
(2) Switch to Elena Voss. Mark D-004 in repair. Switch back to Sam and attempt to check out Maya's D-004 reservation through the UI and via a forged request that still carries a live scan if one is required. Both must be refused — a paid booking still fails at the door once the unit is in the repair bay. Leave D-004 confirmed.
(3) Switch to Maya Chen. Forge a check-out request against her own already-closed L-118 reservation only. A customer must not be able to check a kit out.
Fail if D-004 or T-012 is or becomes checked out, if step 1 was only a scan-first 422, or if a customer identity can check gear out.

criteria.name: concurrent_double_submit_one_paper
criteria.description:
The counter double-clicks. The customer gets one hire.
This is a RACE, not a sequence: the two requests must be in flight at the same time.
Issue them from the page's own origin with a single JavaScript evaluation that fires
both and awaits them together (`Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled` over two `fetch`
calls started before either resolves). Two calls one after the other do not test this
and must not be recorded as a pass.
(1) As Maya, fire TWO simultaneous confirm-and-pay requests for the SAME already-paid
Stripe session for D-004. Exactly one may result in a reservation. Re-read Maya's
reservations and confirm there is exactly ONE D-004 row, not two, and that she was
charged once.
(2) Fire TWO simultaneous booking requests, as two DIFFERENT customers (Maya and
Jordan Hale, using their own identities), for the SAME unit K-055 over the SAME dates
2030-11-25 through 2030-11-27. At most one may end up holding that unit. If both
receive a Checkout URL, follow neither — but the app must not be able to end up with
two live papers on one unit for overlapping days. Abandon both.
(3) Re-read the log as Elena: the double-submit in (1) must have produced ONE line,
not two.
Fail if two rows, two charges, two log lines, or two live papers on one unit resulted
— and fail if you did not actually issue the requests concurrently.

criteria.name: three_books_reconcile_to_the_penny
criteria.description:
Stripe, the shop ledger, and what the customer was told are the same figures.
Take D-004, Maya's paid drone hire (2030-07-01..03, Downtown).
(1) STRIPE — open the Checkout session that paid for it and record the amount
actually charged, and the line breakdown.
(2) THE LEDGER — read the reservation from the app and record its total, its tax, its
hull rider, and its held deposit.
(3) THE COPY DESKS — read the receipt/notice desks for that hire and record the total
the customer was told.
All three must agree to the penny: about $939.20 total, with the $45.00 hull rider
and the $500.00 deposit appearing in each. A figure that is right in the ledger and
rounded, truncated, or recomputed differently on the notice is a fail — the customer
was told something the till cannot back.
(4) Repeat the three-way check for T-012 (about $322.92) and confirm those agree too.
Fail if any of the three sources disagrees with the others by any amount, if a
source is missing the hull rider or the deposit, or if a desk reports a total it
recomputed rather than the one charged.

criteria.name: manager_restores_from_repair_bay
criteria.description:
Kit comes back from the repair bay by the manager's hand and nobody else's.
Use W-044, the Riverside wireless kit that is in repair.
(1) POSITIVE CONTROL — confirm W-044 is currently NOT bookable: as Maya, attempt to
quote it for 2030-10-14 through 2030-10-16 and confirm it is refused.
(2) REFUSALS — as Sam Ortiz (associate), then as Riley Chen (damage assessor), then as
Maya (customer), attempt to restore W-044 to the floor, first through the UI where a
control exists and then as a forged direct request. All must be refused, and W-044 must
still read as in repair after each.
(3) THE MANAGER — switch to Elena Voss and restore W-044 through the manager's own
control. This must succeed and W-044 must read as available.
(4) It is ordinary floor stock again: as Maya, quote W-044 for those same dates. It must
now be ACCEPTED. Abandon without paying.
Fail if any non-manager restore succeeded, if the manager's restore was refused, if
W-044 was bookable before the restore, or if it is still unbookable after it.

criteria.name: restore_blocked_while_spoken_for
criteria.description:
The manager cannot pull a unit back onto the floor while it is spoken for.
Run this AFTER `manager_restores_from_repair_bay` and BEFORE
`customer_cancel_releases_deposit` — it needs T-012 still promised to a live paper.
T-012 is Maya's paid tent, CONFIRMED and not yet gone out, so its unit is promised.
As Elena Voss, attempt to put T-012's unit back on the floor, through the UI where a
control exists and then as a forged direct request. It must be refused while that
paper is live.
Re-read afterwards: T-012's unit must be unchanged and still promised, and Maya's
T-012 reservation must still be CONFIRMED with its deposit still held.
POSITIVE CONTROL — the refusal must be about the live paper and not about the manager
being powerless. Confirm W-044, restored in the previous criterion, still reads as
available. If it does not, the manager's restore never worked and this criterion
fails.
Do NOT probe D-004 here: it is sitting in the repair bay from an earlier criterion,
which is a different state with a different answer.
Fail if the restore succeeded, if T-012's unit or reservation changed, or if the
W-044 control shows the manager's restore never worked.

criteria.name: customer_cancel_releases_deposit
criteria.description:
A paid paper that has not gone out can be called off by the customer who holds it,
and the whole deposit comes back.
Use T-012, Maya's paid tent for 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23, which is CONFIRMED and
has NOT been checked out. Do not use L-118 or D-004.
(1) As Maya, call the T-012 paper off through the app's own control. This must succeed
and the reservation must read as cancelled.
(2) Re-read it: the ENTIRE held deposit of about $80.00 must show as released, with
nothing captured. Not part of it, not a fee retained — all of it.
(3) Re-read T-012's unit card: it must be back on the floor as available, bookable
again. As Maya, quote T-012 for those same 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23 dates and
confirm the app now accepts it. Abandon without paying.
(4) Send the same cancel request twice more by forged direct request. The reservation
must stay cancelled with the deposit released exactly once — no second release, no
change to the released figure.
Fail if the cancel is refused, if any part of the deposit is retained or captured, if
the unit does not return to the floor, if the re-quote in step (3) is refused, or if a
repeat cancel released money a second time or altered the row.

criteria.name: cancel_scope_and_state_gate
criteria.description:
Calling off is the paper-holder's own act, and only while the kit is still on the shelf.
Run this AFTER `customer_cancel_releases_deposit`.
(1) STATE GATE — L-118's paper is no longer a live booking waiting on the shelf: it has
gone out, come back, and been through the damage flow. As Maya, attempt to call it off,
through the UI where a control exists and then as a forged direct request. It must be
refused — only a paid paper that has not gone out can be called off. Re-read L-118 and
confirm the attempt changed nothing: same status, same deposit figures as before you
tried.
(2) OWNERSHIP — switch to Jordan Hale and forge a cancel against Maya's D-004 paper,
which is still CONFIRMED. It must be refused and D-004 must be unchanged.
(3) STAFF — switch to Sam Ortiz, then to Elena Voss, and forge the same cancel against
Maya's D-004 paper from each. Both must be refused; the counter and the manager do not
call off a customer's hire for them. D-004 must still be CONFIRMED with its deposit held.
Switch back to Maya afterwards.
Fail if any of these four probes succeeded, if D-004's or L-118's stored state changed,
or if any deposit figure moved. A 404 that hides the record from a stranger counts as a
refusal for probe (2); a 403 counts for (3).

criteria.name: audit_log_records_the_decisions
criteria.description:
Every decision that moves kit, money, or a customer's standing leaves a line in the log.
Run this LAST, after the counter, damage, cancel and repair-bay work is finished.
As Elena Voss, open the shop's log of who did what and read it.
(1) It must carry a line for each of these things that actually happened in this run:
the confirmation of a paid paper, the hand-over of kit at the counter, the taking of it
back in, the clearing of an inspection, the filing of a damage report, a unit going into
the repair bay, a unit coming back out of it, a wall-card rate change, a customer being
put on hold, and the paper that was called off. Quote the lines you find.
(2) Each line must identify WHO did it, WHAT they did, and WHICH record it touched, and
must carry the record's state before and after where the action changed a state. A log
that records only a timestamp and a free-text sentence does not satisfy this.
(3) The actor must be the person who actually did it. Spot-check three lines against
what you did earlier in this run — the rate change must be attributed to Elena, the
hand-over to Sam, the damage filing to Riley — and confirm the log does not attribute
everything to one default identity.
Fail if any of the ten actions is missing, if lines do not carry actor / action /
entity, or if the actor is wrong or is the same identity throughout.

criteria.name: audit_log_read_gate
criteria.description:
The log is the manager's and the night auditor's, and it is a record rather than a
workspace.
(1) POSITIVE CONTROL — as Elena Voss (manager) and then as Harper Singh (night auditor),
read the log. BOTH must succeed and return entries. If either is refused, this criterion
fails: an app that hides the log from everyone has not implemented a gate.
(2) REFUSALS — as Sam Ortiz (associate), Riley Chen (assessor), Wei Tan (insurance
liaison), and Maya Chen (customer), attempt the same read, first through the UI where a
control exists and then as a forged direct request. All four must be refused with an
error status and no log entries in the body.
(3) READING NEVER WRITES — as Harper, re-read the log twice and confirm the entry count
is unchanged and no new line was created by the act of reading. Then, as Harper, forge a
write against the log — an attempt to insert, edit, or delete an entry. It must be
refused, and the count must still be unchanged.
Fail if either permitted reader was refused, if any of the four refused roles obtained
entries, if reading created a line, or if Harper could alter the log.

criteria.name: idempotency_key_required_on_writes
criteria.description:
Nothing that changes anything is done without a ticket number.
Probe FIVE mutating routes, spread across roles, each as a forged direct request
carrying NO Idempotency-Key header at all:
(1) as Maya, start a booking for L-118 over 2030-12-02 through 2030-12-04;
(2) as Sam Ortiz, a check-out against any live reservation;
(3) as Elena Voss, a wall-card rate change on K-055;
(4) as Elena Voss, put Jordan Hale on hold;
(5) as Riley Chen, file a damage report.
Every one must be refused with a 4xx that is specifically about the missing header.
Then confirm nothing moved: probe (1) returned no Checkout URL and no session id;
K-055's daily rate is unchanged; Jordan is not on hold; no new damage report exists;
no kit changed hands. Read the shop's log as Elena and confirm none of these five
left a line.
POSITIVE CONTROL — the refusals must be about the missing ticket number, not about
the acts being impossible. Repeat probe (3), the K-055 rate change, with a fresh
Idempotency-Key. It must now be ACCEPTED and the rate must change. (Set it back
afterwards with another fresh key.)
READS ARE UNAFFECTED — as Maya, read reservations and read the catalog with no
Idempotency-Key. Both must succeed.
Fail if any of the five keyless writes was accepted, if any state changed, if the
keyed retry of (3) was refused, or if a keyless read was refused.

criteria.name: idempotent_replay_returns_same_answer
criteria.description:
The same ticket number twice does the act once and answers the same way twice.
(1) THE SIDE EFFECT HAPPENS ONCE — as Elena Voss, change K-055's wall card to a new
daily rate with an Idempotency-Key you choose and record in full. Send the
byte-identical request again with the SAME key, then a third time. Then read the
shop's log as Elena: there must be exactly ONE `unit.rate` line for K-055 from this
sequence, not two and not three. K-055's rate must equal the new figure, not the new
figure applied repeatedly.
(2) THE ANSWER IS THE SAME ANSWER — each repeat must return the same status and a
body matching the first on every figure and identifier, not merely a similar-looking
fresh one.
(3) A SESSION IS NOT RE-CUT — as Maya, start a booking for L-118 over 2030-12-02
through 2030-12-04 with a key you choose, and record the returned session id and
quote. Send the identical request again with the SAME key. It must return the SAME
Checkout session id and the SAME quote figures — a second, different Stripe session
means the act was performed twice. Abandon without paying.
(4) A replayed key must be ANSWERED, not rejected: none of the repeats above may
come back as an error.
Put K-055's rate back to its original figure afterwards, using a fresh key.
Fail on a second log line, a second Stripe session, a changed figure between the
first answer and a repeat, a compounded rate, or any repeat refused outright.

criteria.name: idempotency_key_scope_and_conflict
criteria.description:
A ticket number names one act, and it belongs to one person.
Run this AFTER `idempotent_replay_returns_same_answer`; it reuses that criterion's
booking key from step (3).
(1) CONFLICT — as Maya, reuse that exact key on a DIFFERENT request: same route, but
K-055 instead of L-118, or different dates. It must be refused as a conflict. It must
NOT be performed as a fresh act, and it must NOT replay the L-118 answer — check the
body: if it comes back carrying the L-118 session id, the app replayed rather than
conflicted, and that is a fail.
(2) DIFFERENT ROUTE, SAME KEY — as Maya, send that same key to a different mutating
route entirely. Refused as a conflict, not performed.
(3) PER-PERSON SCOPE — switch to Jordan Hale and start a booking with that SAME key
string, for a unit and dates of his own that he is entitled to. It must be ACCEPTED
on its own merits. Jordan must never receive Maya's stored answer — check the session
id differs from Maya's — and must not be refused merely because Maya used the string.
Abandon without paying.
(4) A REFUSAL DOES NOT SPEND A KEY — as Maya, with a brand-new key, attempt to book
X-410 (retired). It will be refused on its own merits. Now reuse that same key for a
legitimate L-118 booking over 2030-12-02 through 2030-12-04. It must be ACCEPTED,
because the first attempt never completed. Abandon without paying.
Fail if a conflict probe was accepted or silently replayed, if Jordan received Maya's
session or was refused for her key, or if a key was burned by a refusal.

criteria.name: unknown_identity_rejected
criteria.description:
An identity that matches nobody in the shop is turned away rather than quietly becoming the default customer. Determine how the active identity travels (a header, a cookie, a body field, or a value in browser storage). Then issue the app's own reads and writes with that identity set to values that match no seeded person: a well-formed but unseeded UUID, the literal string "admin", the literal string "customer", and a seeded EMAIL address used where an id is expected if the app keys on ids. Do NOT test an absent or empty identity — a fresh browser with no identity set is required to open as Maya Chen, so that case is correct behaviour rather than a leak. For each, attempt to read reservations and to create a booking. Every one must be
refused with an error status.
EVIDENCE — a rendered page is NOT evidence here. If you change a stored identity
value, the page you are looking at still holds whatever it fetched under the previous
identity until it reloads; Maya's reservations still on screen after you edited
storage tells you nothing about what the server did. Judge this criterion only on the
status code and body of a request you issued yourself. Record, for each of the four
values, the exact value you sent and the exact HTTP status you got back. If you
cannot produce a status code for all four, record UNREACHED rather than a failure —
do not infer a leak from what the page was displaying.
(5) THE OMITTED IDENTITY — this is a REQUIRED probe, not an optional one. Issue a
request that carries NO identity at all: no `x-demo-user-id` header, no cookie, no
query parameter, nothing. Confirm from the actual outgoing request that the header is
genuinely absent rather than empty. Ask for reservations and then attempt a booking.
Both must be refused. An app that serves Maya Chen — or any customer — to a caller
who never said who they were has a default-identity fallback, and that is the
headline failure of this criterion.
Fail if any unknown identity, or the omitted identity, is served Maya's reservations,
is served any customer's data, or can create a booking. Falling back to a default
customer is the specific failure this criterion is looking for.
Also: as Maya, forge a booking for L-118 on a free midweek span (2030-10-07 through 2030-10-09). In THE SAME request include customer_id, customerId, user_id, userId, owner_id, and ownerId together, all set to Chris Nguyen's seeded id. Do not send only one spelling. If the server accepts it, follow the Checkout URL and verify the session is Maya's (maya.chen@example.com, L-118, about $544.79), not Chris's. Abandon without paying. Switch to Chris and confirm his reservations are still empty. Switch back to Maya: no unpaid L-118 row for those dates.
