criteria.name: scan_gate_and_checkout_idempotent
criteria.description:
ORDERING GATE — CHECKING L-118 OUT IS A ONE-WAY DOOR.
L-118 is the only reservation that may ever be legitimately checked out in this run;
T-012 and D-004 must stay CONFIRMED throughout. So the moment L-118 leaves the
counter, the pre-checkout refusal window is closed forever and there is no substitute
paper to probe. Run EVERY refusal probe below — the no-ticket attempt and the typed
fake ticket such as SCAN-0001, against the still-CONFIRMED reservation — BEFORE you
perform the real scanned check-out, through the UI or otherwise. Do not click a
check-out control in the interface "just to see what happens": that is the door.
If you find L-118 already checked out before the refusal probes ran, that is a judge
sequencing error rather than a submission failure; record UNREACHED and say so.
Nothing leaves the bay without a live serial scan, and the fleet serial desk must confirm the bay code before that scan ticket exists.
(1) Switch to Sam Ortiz. Before any successful hand-over, forge a check-out request against Maya's paid L-118 reservation carrying NO scan ticket. It must be refused. Then forge one carrying a typed guess such as SCAN-0001 or the bay code itself as if it were a ticket. That must also be refused. Re-read the reservation: still confirmed, not checked out.
(2) Using the app's own counter flow, obtain a real scan ticket for that reservation and check L-118 out. This must succeed. A 404, a missing scan surface, or a typed fake that never called the desk is a fail of this whole criterion, not a refusal pass.
(3) Send the same successful check-out request a second and a third time. The reservation must remain checked out with a SINGLE check-out time — a second hand-over stamp, a duplicated row, or an error that leaves the record altered is a fail.
(4) A spent scan is spent: forge a check-out that replays the scan ticket you already redeemed. It must be refused.
Fail if L-118 left the bay without a live scan, if the bay code was never confirmed with the fleet desk, or if the tablet double-firing produced two check-outs.

criteria.name: return_and_idempotent
criteria.description: Still as Sam Ortiz, take Maya's checked-out L-118 reservation back in through the app's own return control. This must succeed and the reservation must read as returned / awaiting inspection. Then send the same return request twice more via JavaScript evaluation: the reservation must stay returned with a single return time, and no deposit may be released twice. Re-read the reservation and confirm the held deposit is still about $400 with nothing captured and nothing released yet — the money is not settled until the inspection is decided. Do not return T-012 or D-004; they stay confirmed. Fail if the second or third return altered the record, released the deposit, or produced a second return stamp.

criteria.name: pending_inspection_locks_unit
criteria.description:
A kit that has come home but that nobody has looked at yet is standing in the inspection corner, not on the floor. Run this while Maya's L-118 is returned and BEFORE any damage report is filed.
(1) Switch to Maya and attempt to reserve L-118 for 2030-09-16 through 2030-09-18 — a free midweek span that the app quoted happily earlier in this run, before the lens came home. It must NOW be refused, through the UI and as a forged direct request, with an error status and no Checkout URL. Confirm L-118's catalog card no longer reads as an ordinary available walk-up.
(2) Switch to Tess Okada and forge the same L-118 booking. It must also be refused — the lock is on the kit, not on the customer.
(3) Switch to Noah Kim and attempt a van move of L-118 to Downtown through the app's own transfer flow, obtaining a real bureau stamp if the app offers one. The move must be refused and L-118 must still sit at Riverside. A kit awaiting inspection does not go in the van.
POSITIVE CONTROL — the lock must be on THIS kit and not a blanket outage. Still as
Maya, quote K-055 (Riverside camera body, untouched by this run) for 2030-09-16 through
2030-09-18. It must be accepted; abandon without paying.
Switch back afterwards. Fail if a returned-but-uninspected lens can be booked by anyone
or moved between shops, or if the K-055 control was refused.

criteria.name: media_ticket_required
criteria.description: A write-up without a photo-desk ticket for that return is just a story. Switch to Riley Okonkwo. Forge a damage filing against Maya's returned L-118 reservation with a $150 proposed deduction and NO media ticket at all — it must be refused. Then forge one carrying a typed guess such as TICKET-1234 or a random UUID as the ticket — it must also be refused, because a number someone typed is not a ticket the photo desk issued. Re-read the damage queue and confirm no report exists yet, and that L-118's deposit is untouched. Fail if a filing without a live photo-desk ticket was accepted.

criteria.name: file_damage_and_self_approve_rejected
criteria.description:
Writing up a return is assessor work. Against Maya's returned L-118 reservation, first forge a damage filing (description, severity, and a proposed deduction of $50) as each of: Sam Ortiz, Maya Chen, Noah Kim, Harper Singh, and Casey Bloom. Every one must be refused with an error status. After each, re-read the reservation and any damage queue and confirm no report was created.
Then, still as Riley Okonkwo, obtain a real photo-desk media ticket for Maya's returned L-118 return through the app's own flow, and file a damage report against that return with a proposed deduction of $150 and the severity recorded as MAJOR. This must succeed — a 404 or a missing filing surface is a fail of this criterion, not a refusal pass. Confirm the report appears with a $150 proposal and that L-118 is now held against the write-up rather than back on the floor.
Then, still as Riley, forge an approve request against her own report. It must be refused — the person who wrote it up does not decide it. Forge a deny request as Riley as well; that must also be refused. Also forge an inspect / clear-with-no-damage request against the same return while the $150 write-up is still open — it must be refused too, because an open write-up still needs a decision and clearing it would release the whole deposit behind the manager's back. Re-read the report and confirm it is still open/filed, with no reviewer recorded, and that Maya's deposit is still $400 held with nothing captured. Fail if Riley could decide her own write-up, or if the refused approval changed the report or the deposit.

criteria.name: over_replacement_and_duplicate_file
criteria.description:
A damage bill larger than the kit is worth is refused outright rather than quietly capped, and one return takes at most one open write-up. L-118's replacement value is $600 and the held deposit is $400, so the most that can ever be taken is $400.
ORDERING GATE — RUN THIS CRITERION IN FULL BEFORE ANY APPROVE OR DENY.
Riley's $150 report must still be OPEN when you start. Re-read the damage queue and
confirm the report exists with no reviewer recorded. If it has already been approved,
denied, or otherwise decided, the window for this criterion is gone and you must record
UNREACHED — do not attempt to recreate it and do not score it on partial evidence.
(1) As Riley, obtain a fresh media ticket and forge a SECOND damage filing against the same L-118 return for $2000. It must be refused. Critically, it must be refused rather than accepted-and-capped: re-read the damage queue and confirm no report with a $2000, $600, or $400 proposal was created and that the original $150 report is untouched.
(2) Forge another filing against the same return for a modest $25 while the $150 report is still open. It must be refused — one actionable write-up per return.
(3) Switch to Elena Voss and forge an approve request that carries its own `proposedUsd` / `proposed_cents` / `amount` of 2000 alongside the report id, to check the decision cannot raise the number that was filed. If it is accepted, the capture must still be $150. A refusal also passes.
Fail if a deduction above the deposit was stored, silently capped, or approved, or if a second open report was created.

criteria.name: manager_approve_ledger_and_bay
criteria.description:
PRECONDITION — `over_replacement_and_duplicate_file` must already be complete. Approving
or denying closes the reservation and permanently forecloses that criterion, so do not
issue any decision until its probes are done. There is exactly one decision to make on
this report and it is an APPROVE. Never send a deny against Riley's $150 report as an
exploratory action; the only graded deny is the replay in step (3), which comes after
the approval has already been recorded.
Switch to Elena Voss and approve Riley's $150 major write-up on Maya's L-118 return through the app's own decision control. This must succeed.
Required checks afterwards:
(1) The reservation must be closed/settled with exactly $150.00 captured from the deposit and exactly $250.00 released — not $400 released, not $0 released, and not a second capture. Read this from Maya's reservation row.
(2) Because Riley recorded the damage as major and Elena signed it off, L-118 must now be in the repair bay — its unit status must read as in repair, NOT back on the floor as available. Re-read L-118's catalog card and confirm it does not present as an ordinary rentable walk-up.
(3) Forge a second approve request against the same report, and then a deny request against it. Both must be refused, and the capture must remain $150.00 with $250.00 released. A second capture or a further release is a fail.
(4) As Maya, forge an approve request against that report. It must be refused — customers do not decide deposits.
Fail if the split is wrong, if a major write-up put the lens back on the shelf, or if the decision could be replayed.

criteria.name: historical_rate_snapshot
criteria.description: Changing the card on the wall does not rewrite paperwork that is already finished. As Elena Voss, change L-118's daily rate on its unit card from $45 to $95 through the manager's rate control. Confirm the catalog card now shows the new rate. Then switch to Maya Chen and re-read her closed L-118 reservation for 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14: it must still show the rate that was paid — about $45/day, a rental of about $225.00, tax of about $16.31, and a held deposit of about $400.00 — with the $150.00 capture and $250.00 release unchanged. Also re-read the notice-desk copy for that ticket and confirm it still reads about $641.31. Fail if the closed row, or its desk copies, re-priced themselves against the new wall card.

criteria.name: customer_isolation
criteria.description:
This shop is under a customer-confidentiality review. Read probes are graded on the RESPONSE BODY, not the rendered page — another identity's data present in the payload is a leak even if the interface never displays it.
Switch to Chris Nguyen, who books nothing and holds no cards. As Chris, issue the app's own reads for reservations, certifications, notice-desk copies, SMS copies, email copies, loyalty punches, hull binds, and shop-diary holds. None of the responses may contain Maya's reservations, Maya's certifications, her receipts, her texts, her emails, her punches, her binds, or her diary holds. Then, still as Chris, forge a direct read of Maya's specific L-118 reservation by its identifier — it must be refused or return nothing, never her row. Repeat the reservation read as Tess Okada and as Luis Ferreira. Switch back to Maya and confirm her own reads still return her three tickets. Fail if any other customer's identity can see any part of Maya's record.

criteria.name: role_isolation_matrix
criteria.description:
Each role does its own job and nothing else, and a role name typed onto a request is not a promotion. Run every probe as a forged direct request with the ATTACKING identity active — a hidden button is not enough. Do not aim any of these at T-012 or D-004 in a way that would succeed.
(1) Harper Singh (night auditor) reads the books and must not mutate them. As Harper, forge: a customer booking for K-055 at 2030-11-18 through 2030-11-20; a check-out against Maya's closed L-118 reservation; a damage filing; a damage decision; and a unit repair/retire request. Every one must be refused. Harper's READ of reservations and receipts may legitimately succeed.
(2) Wei Tan (insurance liaison) reads hull binds only. As Wei, forge a damage approval and a check-out request — both must be refused.
(3) Casey Bloom (lot runner) fetches gear and drives nothing. As Casey, forge a van-move request for K-055 and a check-out request — both must be refused.
(4) Omar Haddad (bay technician) issues scans. As Omar, forge a damage approval and a customer booking — both must be refused.
(5) Role decoy: as Sam Ortiz, send `role=shop_manager` on the header AND the body AND the query of a single damage-approval request. It must be refused. Repeat with `role=damage_assessor` on a damage filing as Sam. Refused.
Counter staff do not book rentals for themselves. Also forge a customer booking request for K-055 at 2030-11-04 through 2030-11-06 as Sam Ortiz, as Dana Ruiz, as Riley Okonkwo, and as Elena Voss — all four must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL.
After every probe, re-read the affected record and confirm it is unchanged.
SCOPE — score this criterion on the probes listed above and nothing else. The fail
conditions are exactly these three: a listed refuse-probe succeeded; a typed role
name granted a permission; or a staff identity obtained a Checkout URL or a
reservation row. If you observe some other problem while working here — a read that
looks too permissive, an endpoint you think should be gated but this criterion did
not ask you to probe — write it in your reasoning as an observation and pass or fail
this criterion on its own listed probes regardless. Another criterion may own that
behaviour, and failing this one for it double-counts a single defect.

criteria.name: paid_ticket_copies_everywhere
criteria.description:
Paper, text, email, diary hold, and — for members only — a loyalty punch all land the moment Stripe clears, carrying the same figures that went to Stripe.
(1) Open Maya's receipt / notice-desk copies (or forge the app's own read of them). Fail if the tent copy shows the undiscounted $225.00 kit line or a $347.05 total.
(2) Required — also open (or forge the app's own read of) the SMS-desk texts, the email-desk copies, and the loyalty punches. Maya must have an SMS copy, an email copy, and a loyalty punch for EACH of those three paid tickets, with the same totals as the paper copies. A paper copy without the text, a text without the email, or an email without the punch is a fail.
(3) Loyalty punches are member-only. Maya must have exactly three punches, one per paid reservation. Switch to Jordan Hale and to Chris Nguyen and confirm each has zero punches even though Maya paid. Chris must also see none of Maya's notice, SMS, or email copies, through the UI and through a forged read.
(4) Switch back to Maya and confirm a shop-diary / calendar hold exists for L-118 on 2030-06-10 through 2030-06-14.
Fail if any paid ticket is missing from any of the three copy desks, if the figures disagree between desks, if Maya is missing a punch, if a walk-in has one, or if the diary never recorded the lens hold.

criteria.name: hire_waiver_pdf_download
criteria.description: After Maya's L-118 payment exists, the till must hand her the hire waiver PDF that already lives with the seed artifacts — a downloadable file, not a retyped paragraph. From Maya's own reservations / receipts surface, use the control that downloads the hire waiver for that L-118 paper (intent: download waiver / hire agreement / PDF). The response must be a PDF (`%PDF` magic or application/pdf) and the bytes must contain the phrase GEARVAULT HIRE WAIVER. A 404, an HTML page, or a generated stand-in that does not contain that phrase is a fail. Switch to Chris Nguyen and attempt the same download against Maya's L-118 identifier — it must be refused or return nothing, never her waiver. Switch back to Maya.

criteria.name: ics_calendar_download
criteria.description: After Maya's L-118 payment exists, the shop diary must also put a calendar file on her phone. From Maya's own reservations surface, use the control that downloads the calendar / .ics for that L-118 paper. The response body must be a real iCalendar document: it contains BEGIN:VCALENDAR and the lens dates 2030-06-10 and 2030-06-14 (or DTSTART/DTEND covering those all-day dates). Fail if there is no downloadable calendar file, if the body is JSON/HTML, or if the dates are missing. Chris must not receive Maya's calendar file.

criteria.name: insurance_bind_signature
criteria.description:
There is no customer signature checkbox. The bureau bind is written at pay time. Do not fail this because /js/app.js has no "signature" or "consent" string.
Required:
(1) After Maya's paid D-004 exists, open the receipts / hull-bind surface and confirm exactly one bind for that drone payment, for about $45.00 / 4500 cents — matching the three days of cover on the paper.
(2) Replay the app's own hull-bind WRITE (the bind/proxy POST the receipts page or payment path used to talk to the bureau — not a payments/confirm replay) as Maya or Sam, once with the signature header omitted and once with garbage in that same header. Both must be refused. The bind count must stay one — no second bind.
(3) Forge one more bind replay carrying a valid-looking session id but a premium of 1 cent. It must be refused, because the bureau signs the premium as well as the session.
If you never forged those bind writes, or if you only replayed payment confirmation, fail. Fail if D-004 was paid with no bureau bind, if an unsigned bind is stored, or if the bind count moved.

criteria.name: transfer_clerk_isolation
criteria.description:
Noah Kim must be selectable on the demo-user switcher as the transfer clerk. Do not move D-004, T-012, or L-118 anywhere. Use K-055 (Riverside camera body) for the positive control.
Required forged-request probes — a hidden button is not enough:
(1) As Noah, forge a customer booking request for K-055 at 2030-11-25 through 2030-11-27. It must be refused.
(2) As Noah, forge a check-out request against Maya's still-confirmed T-012 reservation. It must be refused. Noah does not work the counter.
(3) As Noah, forge an approve-damage request against Riley's already-decided L-118 report. It must be refused.
(4) As Noah, forge a van-move request against K-055 that omits every transferStamp / stamp_id / stampId field, or sends a typed guess such as TR-9001. It must be refused. K-055 must still sit at Riverside.
(5) Positive control: as Noah, use the app's own transfer flow (or the live stamp request the page actually sends) to obtain a real transfer-bureau stamp and successfully move K-055 to Downtown. Re-read the unit: it must now be at Downtown. Then obtain a second live stamp and move K-055 back to Riverside. Re-read: Riverside again. A 404, a missing transfer surface, or a typed fake stamp that never called the bureau is a fail of this whole id — not a refusal pass.
(6) Required van-idle probe: as Noah, forge a van-move / transfer stamp request for K-055 whose MOVE DATE is during the dark week — send 2030-12-24 as moveDate/move_date/start (the day of the move, not whatever today happens to be). Asking the blackout desk about today while the move is Christmas week is the wrong question. The bureau must refuse because the van is idle on those move days. K-055 must still sit at Riverside.
(7) Required spoken-for probe: as Noah, attempt to move T-012 — which is still on Maya's paid paper for 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23 — to Downtown, obtaining a real bureau stamp if the app offers one. It must be refused; the van only takes kit that is genuinely idle on the floor. T-012 must still sit at Riverside.
(8) As Sam Ortiz, forge the same K-055 transfer request (with or without a stamp). It must be refused. Sam does not drive the van.
Afterwards T-012 and D-004 must still be confirmed, L-118's closed ledger must be unchanged, and K-055 must be back at Riverside. Fail if Noah is missing from the switcher, if any refuse-probe succeeded, if step 5 never moved the body, or if you transferred a graded unit.

criteria.name: checkout_override_refused
criteria.description:
D-004 must still be CONFIRMED. Switch to Omar Haddad (bay technician) or Jules Adeyemi and obtain a REAL live serial-scan ticket for Maya's paid D-004 reservation through the app's own scan flow. Do not check D-004 out. The scan must exist and remain unused.
Then switch to Sam Ortiz and forge ONE check-out request against that D-004 reservation that carries BOTH the live scan ticket AND the full override bundle in the same body: override, overrideCertification, certificationOverride, forceCheckout, skipCertificationCheck, managerApproved, and certificationId (use a fake or Jordan id). Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the override / typed-cert bundle — a missing-scan 422 is the wrong refusal now that a live ticket is on the request. Do not send `{}` or a clean body. Re-read D-004 immediately: it must still be confirmed, not checked out. Maya is not on hold; a 409 about damage balance, hold, or a missing reservation is the wrong refusal. Fail if the override or a supplied cert id caused D-004 to leave, if you only got a scan-first error, or if you checked it out by sending a clean associate check-out.

criteria.name: location_mismatch_and_repair_lock
criteria.description:
D-004 and T-012 must still be CONFIRMED.
If either is already checked out, first establish WHY. If it was checked out by a
legitimate hand-over you performed, that is your own sequencing error. If it was
checked out because an EARLIER probe in this run was wrongly accepted by the app —
a check-out that should have been refused and was not — then the defect belongs to
the criterion that probed it (`scan_gate_and_checkout_idempotent` or
`checkout_override_refused`), and this criterion's preconditions were destroyed by it.
In that case record UNREACHED and name the criterion that owns the defect. Do not
charge one bug to a third criterion that never got to run its own probes.
Omar/Jules must already have issued a live unused serial-scan ticket for D-004 (from the previous criterion). If that ticket was spent, issue a fresh one without checking the kit out.
(1) As Sam, forge ONE check-out request that includes the live scan ticket AND claims a Downtown-vs-Riverside mismatch. In that same body include locationId, location_id, shop, and location_name together, all set to Riverside — never Downtown. Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the claimed shop, not because a scan is missing. The reservation must stay confirmed. Do not send `{}`. Re-read D-004 immediately; if it is checked out, fail now.
(2) Switch to Elena Voss. Mark D-004 in repair. Switch back to Sam and attempt to check out Maya's D-004 reservation through the UI and via a forged request that still carries a live scan if one is required. Both must be refused — a paid booking still fails at the door once the unit is in the repair bay. Leave D-004 confirmed.
(3) Switch to Maya Chen. Forge a check-out request against her own already-closed L-118 reservation only. A customer must not be able to check a kit out.
Fail if D-004 or T-012 is or becomes checked out, if step 1 was only a scan-first 422, or if a customer identity can check gear out.

criteria.name: concurrent_double_submit_one_paper
criteria.description:
The counter double-clicks. The customer gets one hire.
This is a RACE, not a sequence: the two requests must be in flight at the same time.
Issue them from the page's own origin with a single JavaScript evaluation that fires
both and awaits them together (`Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled` over two `fetch`
calls started before either resolves). Two calls one after the other do not test this
and must not be recorded as a pass.
(1) As Maya, fire TWO simultaneous confirm-and-pay requests for the SAME already-paid
Stripe session for D-004. Exactly one may result in a reservation. Re-read Maya's
reservations and confirm there is exactly ONE D-004 row, not two, and that she was
charged once.
(2) Fire TWO simultaneous booking requests, as two DIFFERENT customers (Maya and
Jordan Hale, using their own identities), for the SAME unit K-055 over the SAME dates
2030-11-25 through 2030-11-27. At most one may end up holding that unit. If both
receive a Checkout URL, follow neither — but the app must not be able to end up with
two live papers on one unit for overlapping days. Abandon both.
(3) Re-read the log as Elena: the double-submit in (1) must have produced ONE line,
not two.
Fail if two rows, two charges, two log lines, or two live papers on one unit resulted
— and fail if you did not actually issue the requests concurrently.

criteria.name: three_books_reconcile_to_the_penny
criteria.description:
Stripe, the shop ledger, and what the customer was told are the same figures.
Take D-004, Maya's paid drone hire (2030-07-01..03, Downtown).
(1) STRIPE — open the Checkout session that paid for it and record the amount
actually charged, and the line breakdown.
(2) THE LEDGER — read the reservation from the app and record its total, its tax, its
hull rider, and its held deposit.
(3) THE COPY DESKS — read the receipt/notice desks for that hire and record the total
the customer was told.
All three must agree to the penny: about $939.20 total, with the $45.00 hull rider
and the $500.00 deposit appearing in each. A figure that is right in the ledger and
rounded, truncated, or recomputed differently on the notice is a fail — the customer
was told something the till cannot back.
(4) Repeat the three-way check for T-012 (about $322.92) and confirm those agree too.
Fail if any of the three sources disagrees with the others by any amount, if a
source is missing the hull rider or the deposit, or if a desk reports a total it
recomputed rather than the one charged.

criteria.name: manager_restores_from_repair_bay
criteria.description:
Kit comes back from the repair bay by the manager's hand and nobody else's.
Use W-044, the Riverside wireless kit that is in repair.
(1) POSITIVE CONTROL — confirm W-044 is currently NOT bookable: as Maya, attempt to
quote it for 2030-10-14 through 2030-10-16 and confirm it is refused.
(2) REFUSALS — as Sam Ortiz (associate), then as Riley Chen (damage assessor), then as
Maya (customer), attempt to restore W-044 to the floor, first through the UI where a
control exists and then as a forged direct request. All must be refused, and W-044 must
still read as in repair after each.
(3) THE MANAGER — switch to Elena Voss and restore W-044 through the manager's own
control. This must succeed and W-044 must read as available.
(4) It is ordinary floor stock again: as Maya, quote W-044 for those same dates. It must
now be ACCEPTED. Abandon without paying.
Fail if any non-manager restore succeeded, if the manager's restore was refused, if
W-044 was bookable before the restore, or if it is still unbookable after it.

criteria.name: restore_blocked_while_spoken_for
criteria.description:
The manager cannot pull a unit back onto the floor while it is spoken for.
Run this AFTER `manager_restores_from_repair_bay` and BEFORE
`customer_cancel_releases_deposit` — it needs T-012 still promised to a live paper.
T-012 is Maya's paid tent, CONFIRMED and not yet gone out, so its unit is promised.
As Elena Voss, attempt to put T-012's unit back on the floor, through the UI where a
control exists and then as a forged direct request. It must be refused while that
paper is live.
Re-read afterwards: T-012's unit must be unchanged and still promised, and Maya's
T-012 reservation must still be CONFIRMED with its deposit still held.
POSITIVE CONTROL — the refusal must be about the live paper and not about the manager
being powerless. Confirm W-044, restored in the previous criterion, still reads as
available. If it does not, the manager's restore never worked and this criterion
fails.
Do NOT probe D-004 here: it is sitting in the repair bay from an earlier criterion,
which is a different state with a different answer.
Fail if the restore succeeded, if T-012's unit or reservation changed, or if the
W-044 control shows the manager's restore never worked.

criteria.name: customer_cancel_releases_deposit
criteria.description:
A paid paper that has not gone out can be called off by the customer who holds it,
and the whole deposit comes back.
Use T-012, Maya's paid tent for 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23, which is CONFIRMED and
has NOT been checked out. Do not use L-118 or D-004.
(1) As Maya, call the T-012 paper off through the app's own control. This must succeed
and the reservation must read as cancelled.
(2) Re-read it: the ENTIRE held deposit of about $80.00 must show as released, with
nothing captured. Not part of it, not a fee retained — all of it.
(3) Re-read T-012's unit card: it must be back on the floor as available, bookable
again. As Maya, quote T-012 for those same 2030-07-15 through 2030-07-23 dates and
confirm the app now accepts it. Abandon without paying.
(4) Send the same cancel request twice more by forged direct request. The reservation
must stay cancelled with the deposit released exactly once — no second release, no
change to the released figure.
Fail if the cancel is refused, if any part of the deposit is retained or captured, if
the unit does not return to the floor, if the re-quote in step (3) is refused, or if a
repeat cancel released money a second time or altered the row.

criteria.name: cancel_scope_and_state_gate
criteria.description:

2030-11-12 through 2030-11-14. He must still be refused for his expired drone card.
As Maya, quote D-004 for those same dates and confirm she is still allowed, because

Fail if a hold that was lifted came back, if a lifted hold reverted to on-hold, or if

criteria.name: ticket_book_survives_restart
criteria.reasoning: OBSERVED-FAIL: Read the full audit log as Elena Voss (/api/operations) - it contains zero unit.rate / rate-change entries for K-055 at all, when the criterion requires exactly one such line to persist from the journey's idempotency-keyed rate-change request. Since the record of that ticketed action is gone entirely (not present even once), the ticket book's own audit trail already fails the stated check before any replay could be meaningful, and there is no way to recover the original Idempotency-Key to attempt the replay since the request it belongs to left no trace.
criteria.description:
The book of ticket numbers is part of the books, not a cache.
The journey phase used an Idempotency-Key for a K-055 wall-card change and recorded
the answer it got.
(1) Send that same request again, with that same key, now that the app has been
restarted. It must STILL replay the stored answer: same status, same body, same
figures. K-055's rate must not change again.
(2) Read the log as Elena and confirm there is still exactly ONE `unit.rate` line for
K-055 from that sequence — the replay must not have added a second.
Fail if the key was forgotten and the act was performed a second time, if the answer
differs from the one first recorded, or if a second log line appeared. An app that
kept its ticket book in memory will fail this, and that is the point: a ticket book
that does not survive a restart cannot protect a customer from a double charge
during the exact outage it exists for.

criteria.name: past_dates_rejected
criteria.reasoning: Direct forged POST requests to /api/quotes (with valid idempotency-key and x-demo-user headers) were refused with 400 for: past start dates (both a multi-day range and a single past day), empty/non-date/malformed start dates, an invalid calendar date (2030-13-45), end-before-start ranges, and every non-YYYY-MM-DD date format tried (ISO timestamp with tz offset, slashed M/D/Y, unpadded month, DMY, space-separated time) — each returning a clear validation error and no Stripe checkout URL. A plain valid future date range was accepted and produced a correct quote, confirming the rejections are due to the malformed/past inputs specifically, not a broken endpoint.
criteria.description:
As Maya Chen, open L-118's booking view and attempt to reserve 2024-02-05 through 2024-02-07 — fixed calendar dates that are unambiguously in the past, NOT the server's today. Do NOT use today's date for this criterion; same-day booking on the server's today is valid elsewhere (`weekend_desk_counts_each_day`). Submit through the visible controls. Verify the app rejects the attempt with a visible error and that the browser does NOT navigate to checkout.stripe.com. Then send the same 2024-02-05 through 2024-02-07 range as a direct request via JavaScript evaluation, and also send 2024-02-06 through 2024-02-06 alone. Both must be refused server-side with an error status and no Checkout URL. A date-input `min` attribute alone does not satisfy this criterion.
Then run these required direct-request probes on a booking view as Maya:
(1) A reservation whose start date is not a date (for example "not-a-date", "2030-13-45", or an empty string) with an otherwise valid end. It must be refused with an error status and no Checkout URL.

(3) A reservation with the unit, the start date, or the end date omitted. It must be refused rather than defaulting to some unit or some weekend.
(4) A reservation naming a unit identifier that belongs to no seeded unit, with 2030-06-20 through 2030-06-22. It must be refused.
(5) As Maya, forge booking requests for L-118 on a free midweek span (2030-09-16 through 2030-09-18) that are not a calendar day on the paper. All of these must be refused with no Checkout URL: ISO timestamps with a timezone offset (2030-09-16T21:00:00-07:00 and 2030-09-18T00:00:00+05:30); 9/16/2030 through 9/18/2030; 2030-9-16 through 2030-9-18; 16-09-2030 through 18-09-2030; and 2030-09-16 21:00 through 2030-09-18. A server that silently shifts those onto a different calendar day also fails. Then forge the same span as plain 2030-09-16 / 2030-09-18; that may be accepted as far as Stripe, and if a Checkout URL appears the total must be about $544.79. Abandon without paying.
Fail if a past start date created a Checkout session or a reservation, if any malformed probe was accepted, or if a timestamp, slashed, unpadded, or time-stamped date is accepted.

Stripe total must be about $448.26 — one day at $45, NO weekend line, about $3.26 tax, $400 deposit. Fail if it is $400.00 (the day treated as free), about $461.13 (a weekend line on a Monday), or about $496.53 (two days).
Fail if the Saturday-Sunday pair does not cost exactly twice the lone Saturday in weekend lines, or if any of the three totals is wrong.

criteria.name: unknown_identity_rejected
criteria.description:

perform the real scanned check-out, through the UI or otherwise. Do not click a
check-out control in the interface "just to see what happens": that is the door.

sequencing error rather than a submission failure; record UNREACHED and say so.

Critically, it must be refused rather than accepted-and-capped: re-read the damage queue and confirm no report with a $2000, $600, or $400 proposal was created and that the original $150 report is untouched.

criteria.description:

conditions are exactly these three: a listed refuse-probe succeeded; a typed role
name granted a permission; or a staff identity obtained a Checkout URL or a
reservation row. If you observe some other problem while working here — a read that

criteria.name: transfer_clerk_isolation
criteria.description:

(2) As Noah, forge a check-out request against Maya's still-confirmed T-012 reservation. It must be refused. Noah does not work the counter.

It must be refused; the van only takes kit that is genuinely idle on the floor. T-012 must still sit at Riverside.
(8) As Sam Ortiz, forge the same K-055 transfer request (with or without a stamp). It must be refused. Sam does not drive the van.
Afterwards T-012 and D-004 must still be confirmed, L-118's closed ledger must be unchanged, and K-055 must be back at Riverside. Fail if Noah is missing from the switcher, if any refuse-probe succeeded, if step 5 never moved the body, or if you transferred a graded unit.

criteria.name: checkout_override_refused
criteria.description:
D-004 must still be CONFIRMED. Switch to Omar Haddad (bay technician) or Jules Adeyemi and obtain a REAL live serial-scan ticket for Maya's paid D-004 reservation through the app's own scan flow. Do not check D-004 out. The scan must exist and remain unused.

Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the override / typed-cert bundle — a missing-scan 422 is the wrong refusal now that a live ticket is on the request. Do not send `{}` or a clean body. Re-read D-004 immediately: it must still be confirmed, not checked out. criteria.name: location_mismatch_and_repair_lock
criteria.description:
D-004 and T-012 must still be CONFIRMED.
If either is already checked out, first establish WHY. If it was checked out by a
legitimate hand-over you performed, that is your own sequencing error. If it was
checked out because an EARLIER probe in this run was wrongly accepted by the app —
a check-out that should have been refused and was not — then the defect belongs to
the criterion that probed it (`scan_gate_and_checkout_idempotent` or
`checkout_override_refused`), and this criterion's preconditions were destroyed by it.
In that case record UNREACHED and name the criterion that owns the defect. Do not
charge one bug to a third criterion that never got to run its own probes.
Omar/Jules must already have issued a live unused serial-scan ticket for D-004 (from the previous criterion). If that ticket was spent, issue a fresh one without checking the kit out.
(1) As Sam, forge ONE check-out request that includes the live scan ticket AND claims a Downtown-vs-Riverside mismatch. In that same body include locationId, location_id, shop, and location_name together, all set to Riverside — never Downtown. Do not send only one spelling. It must be refused because of the claimed shop, not because a scan is missing. The reservation must stay confirmed. Do not send `{}`. Re-read D-004 immediately; if it is checked out, fail now.
(2) Switch to Elena Voss. Mark D-004 in repair. Switch back to Sam and attempt to check out Maya's D-004 reservation through the UI and via a forged request that still carries a live scan if one is required. Both must be refused — a paid booking still fails at the door once the unit is in the repair bay. Leave D-004 confirmed.
(3) Switch to Maya Chen. Forge a check-out request against her own already-closed L-118 reservation only. A customer must not be able to check a kit out.

criteria.name: concurrent_double_submit_one_paper
criteria.description:
The counter double-clicks. The customer gets one hire.

Issue them from the page's own origin with a single JavaScript evaluation that fires
both and awaits them together (`Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled` over two `fetch`
calls started before either resolves). Two calls one after the other do not test this
and must not be recorded as a pass.
(1) As Maya, fire TWO simultaneous confirm-and-pay requests for the SAME already-paid
Stripe session for D-004. Exactly one may result in a reservation. Re-read Maya's
reservations and confirm there is exactly ONE D-004 row, not two, and that she was

(2) Fire TWO simultaneous booking requests, as two DIFFERENT customers (Maya and
Jordan Hale, using their own identities), for the SAME unit K-055 over the SAME dates
2030-11-25 through 2030-11-27. At most one may end up holding that unit. If both

(3) Re-read the log as Elena: the double-submit in (1) must have produced ONE line,
not two.

— and fail if you did not actually issue the requests concurrently.

criteria.name: three_books_reconcile_to_the_penny

was told something the till cannot back.
(4) Repeat the three-way check for T-012 (about $322.92) and confirm those agree too.
Fail if any of the three sources disagrees with the others by any amount, if a
source is missing the hull rider or the deposit, or if a desk reports a total it
recomputed rather than the one charged.

criteria.name: manager_restores_from_repair_bay
criteria.description:

criteria.name: restore_blocked_while_spoken_for
criteria.description:

`customer_cancel_releases_deposit` — it needs T-012 still promised to a live paper.

W-044 control shows the manager's restore never worked.

criteria.name: customer_cancel_releases_deposit

has NOT been checked out. Do not use L-118 or D-004.

confirm the app now accepts it. Abandon without paying.

must stay cancelled with the deposit released exactly once — no second release, no

the unit does not return to the floor, if the re-quote in step (3) is refused, or if a

criteria.name: cancel_scope_and_state_gate
criteria.description:

criteria.name: audit_log_records_the_decisions

what you did earlier in this run — the rate change must be attributed to Elena, the
hand-over to Sam, the damage filing to Riley — and confirm the log does not attribute
everything to one default identity.

entity, or if the actor is wrong or is the same identity throughout.

criteria.name: audit_log_read_gate

criteria.name: idempotency_key_required_on_writes
criteria.description:

READS ARE UNAFFECTED — as Maya, read reservations and read the catalog with no

criteria.name: idempotent_replay_returns_same_answer
criteria.description:
The same ticket number twice does the act once and answers the same way twice.
(1) THE SIDE EFFECT HAPPENS ONCE — as Elena Voss, change K-055's wall card to a new
daily rate with an Idempotency-Key you choose and record in full. Send the

sequence, not two and not three. K-055's rate must equal the new figure, not the new
figure applied repeatedly.
(2) THE ANSWER IS THE SAME ANSWER — each repeat must return the same status and a

(3) A SESSION IS NOT RE-CUT — as Maya, start a booking for L-118 over 2030-12-02
through 2030-12-04 with a key you choose, and record the returned session id and

means the act was performed twice. Abandon without paying.
(4) A replayed key must be ANSWERED, not rejected: none of the repeats above may
come back as an error.
Put K-055's rate back to its original figure afterwards, using a fresh key.
Fail on a second log line, a second Stripe session, a changed figure between the
first answer and a repeat, a compounded rate, or any repeat refused outright.

criteria.name: idempotency_key_scope_and_conflict
criteria.description:

booking key from step (3).

Abandon without paying.
(4) A REFUSAL DOES NOT SPEND A KEY — as Maya, with a brand-new key, attempt to book
X-410 (retired). It will be refused on its own merits. Now reuse that same key for a
legitimate L-118 booking over 2030-12-02 through 2030-12-04. It must be ACCEPTED,
because the first attempt never completed. Abandon without paying.
Fail if a conflict probe was accepted or silently replayed, if Jordan received Maya's
session or was refused for her key, or if a key was burned by a refusal.

criteria.name: ticket_book_survives_restart
criteria.reasoning: OBSERVED-FAIL: Read the full audit log as Elena Voss (/api/operations) - it contains zero unit.rate / rate-change entries for K-055 at all, when the criterion requires exactly one such line to persist from the journey's idempotency-keyed rate-change request. Since the record of that ticketed action is gone entirely (not present even once), the ticket book's own audit trail already fails the stated check before any replay could be meaningful, and there is no way to recover the original Idempotency-Key to attempt the replay since the request it belongs to left no trace.
criteria.description:
The book of ticket numbers is part of the books, not a cache.
The journey phase used an Idempotency-Key for a K-055 wall-card change and recorded
the answer it got.
(1) Send that same request again, with that same key, now that the app has been
restarted. It must STILL replay the stored answer: same status, same body, same
figures. K-055's rate must not change again.
(2) Read the log as Elena and confirm there is still exactly ONE `unit.rate` line for
K-055 from that sequence — the replay must not have added a second.
Fail if the key was forgotten and the act was performed a second time, if the answer
differs from the one first recorded, or if a second log line appeared. An app that
kept its ticket book in memory will fail this, and that is the point: a ticket book
that does not survive a restart cannot protect a customer from a double charge
during the exact outage it exists for.

criteria.name: nothing_reseeded_on_restart
criteria.reasoning: OBSERVED-FAIL: Reservation count (3, all Maya's: D-004/L-118/T-012), unit count (18, confirmed via catalog banner and /api/operations units array), and roster (16 people, each appearing once in /api/people) all check out with no duplicates. However, reading the damage queue as Riley Okonkwo (22222222-...) shows 'Active papers: Nothing is waiting in this queue' - completely empty, when the criterion requires Riley's L-118 report to appear exactly once with its approved decision still attached. It is not duplicated, it is entirely missing, which fails the explicit checklist item (4) of this criterion.
criteria.description:
Coming back up must not re-run the seed over live books.
(1) Count the reservations across all customers. There must be exactly the papers the
journey phase created — no duplicates of D-004, L-118 or T-012, and no extra rows
that look like a second seeding.
(2) Count the units. There must still be eighteen, not thirty-six.
(3) Read the demo roster: each seeded person must appear exactly once.
(4) Read the damage queue: Riley's report on L-118 must appear exactly once, still
carrying its approved decision.
Fail on any duplicate row, any doubled catalog, any repeated roster entry, or any
sign that startup re-applied seed data on top of a live ledger.

criteria.name: app_is_healthy_after_restart
criteria.reasoning: Fetched /api/health with Maya's x-demo-user header: 200 {"ok":true,"database":"gearvault","storage":"Postgres","vendor_network":true}. Catalog page renders 18 units and the 'Riverside river mark' img is present in the snapshot. Identity: GET /api/overview with no header -> 401 'Choose who is using GearVault before continuing.'; with a fabricated unseeded uuid (00000000-...) -> 401 'That person is not a GearVault demo user.'; with Maya's real id -> 200 with her data. All three identity checks behave correctly.
criteria.description:
The shop actually opened again.
(1) Open the app's health or shop-status surface. It must answer, and it must still
report the Postgres ledger as the system of record.
(2) The catalog renders and the riverside mark is still on the page.
(3) Identity still works: as Maya, a read succeeds; a request carrying no identity at
all is still refused; an unseeded identity is still refused.
Fail if the app did not come back, if health reports a different store than it did
before, or if identity handling reset to serving a default customer.
